Sports.title: Forest in talks with Celta Vigo over Javi Rueda as Axel Disasi joins Palace on loan
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest are in talks over the €15m (£12.8m) signing of the Celta Vigo right-back Javi Rueda, which would probably be their final incoming of the window after Liam Delap from Chelsea.

Oliver Glasner has been seeking someone who can play right wing-back and the 24-year-old former Real Madrid academy player fits the desired profile.

The former Spain youth international joined Celta three years ago from Madrid, who will receive half the fee. He made his first-team breakthrough last season, playing 26 La Liga games and 11 in the Europa League, helping his side to reach the quarter-finals.

Forest confirmed on Wednesday that the wing-back Eric da Silva Moreira will spend the season on loan to the Dutch side Excelsior to aid his development.

Chelsea have agreed to sell Delap to Forest in a deal worth £50m and have loaned Axel Disasi to Crystal Palace for the season. Disasi has also been borrowed by Aston Villa and West Ham since he signed for Chelsea from Monaco.

The defender said: “I know that it’s very tough to play against Palace at Selhurst Park – so I’m looking forward to being on the other side now.”

Brentford have struck an agreement with West Ham to sign El Hadji Malick Diouf for £35m plus up to £5m in add-ons. The left-back has been keen to leave West Ham since their relegation.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and nitrous oxide possession
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on 28 May. The 31-year-old former England forward is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported. Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court for a hearing on 15 September.

Quick Guide How do I 

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate’s side to reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the Euro 2020 final. Sterling came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool, where he made his senior debut and moved in 2015 to Manchester City, with whom he won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup.

Sterling left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour he spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal. After leaving Stamford Bridge, he joined the Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of last season. He is now without a club.

In the 2021 Queen’s birthday honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch.

Sports.title: After Dom Ballard’s backheel, what is the earliest goal of the season? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“After watching Dom Ballard’s backheel volley for Bristol City against Birmingham in game week two of the Championship, it begs the question: what’s the earliest in a season a goal has gone on to win goal of the season?” asks Ricardio Sentulio.

There is no doubting Dom Ballard’s outrageous flick for Bristol City at Birmingham City should be a Puskás contender, especially with his finish kissing the crossbar on its way in, and has a very good chance of being the best goal scored in the 2026-27 Championship season, even though there is a long way to go.

Ballard’s wondergoal was scored on 22 August, on gameweek two. Eleven years ago to that day, Marco Matias notched this ridiculous effort for Sheffield Wednesday at Leeds United, although it should be said that Yorkshire derby was gameweek four, so technically later in the 2015-16 season than Ballard’s. Matias was given the goal of the season gong in April 2016.

The earliest Championship goal of the season we could find was the 2022-23 effort from Ismaïla Sarr for Watford. The Senegalese, now at Palace, scored from the halfway line to stun West Brom on the opening day (8 August). It doesn’t get much earlier, especially as Sarr’s strike was just 12 minutes into the match.

David Beckham’s famous goal for Manchester United against Wimbledon in 1996-97, lobbing Neil Sullivan from the halfway line – later voted the best of that Premier League campaign – was also on the opening day of the league season but came later in the year (11 days after Sarr) and also in the 87th minute (so 75 minutes later than Sarr in the match).

View image in fullscreen A 21-year-old David Beckham, there, on his way to superstardom. Photograph: Tony O’Brien/Action Images/Reuters

In Scotland, the 2017-18 SPFA goal of the season was given to Kieran Tierney for Celtic versus Kilmarnock, also on 8 August (2017) in the League Cup. Even though that is the same date as Sarr’s strike, the cup tie actually came three days after Celtic’s opening league game, a 4-1 win over Hearts on 5 August 2017. We could also mention that Celtic’s Jota once scored a goal of the month (for August even though the goal was in July) for Celtic against Aberdeen (31 July 2022, game one).

We finish with a goal that probably doesn’t quite fit into this category but is too good to ignore or forget. Schalke’s goal of the year (not season, it should be stated) in 2013 came as early as on 27 July but comes with three caveats: a) it was in a pre-season friendly; b) it was by a player that wasn’t even on Schalke’s books at the time of scoring; and c) it was a tap-in.

After two successful years at Schalke, Raúl had joined Al-Sadd, with a pre-season friendly arranged as part of the deal. So when Al-Sadd travelled to Gelsenkirchen on 27 July 2013, Raúl agreed to play the first half for his new side and the second half for Schalke. The Spaniard scored twice for the latter, the first of which was a textbook right-place-right-time finish from two yards out. To understand why it was voted Schalke’s goal of the year, you are going to have to check out the assist from a teenage Julian Draxler.

Have you any earlier examples from further afield? Mail us with your questions and answers.

Spinning plates

“Has a club’s player-manager ever been called up for an international cap, or travelled to play during an international break in the club season?” asks Frederick Sondheimer-Acosta.

Let’s start with a couple of famous examples from the Scotland team of the mid-1980s. “Kenny Dalglish became Liverpool player-manager in the summer of 1985 and subsequently played a few games for Scotland, including the first leg of their World Cup playoff win against Australia,” writes Dom Miller. “He won his 100th cap against Romania in March 1986 and was initially selected for the World Cup squad but withdrew due to a knee injury picked up in the FA Cup final (there has always been a suspicion he didn’t go because his mate Alan Hansen wasn’t picked). Dalglish won his last two caps in the autumn of 1986.”

View image in fullscreen Player-manager Kenny Dalglish (top right) and Liverpool celebrate winning the 1985-86 First Division at Stamford Bridge. Dalglish scored the winning goal to beat Chelsea and clinch the title. Photograph: David Cannon/Getty Images

Scotland, with Alex Ferguson in temporary charge after the tragic death of Jock Stein, did have a player-manager in their squad for the World Cup. Graeme Souness was appointed by Rangers in April and played the first two games at Mexico 86, when Scotland were a little unfortunate to lose to Denmark and West Germany. But Souness struggled with the altitude, saying he never felt worse on a football field than during the West Germany game, and Ferguson left him out of their final group match against Uruguay.

Another mighty, all-purpose midfielder, Johnny Giles, went one better than Souness. “Perhaps uniquely, Giles held player-manager positions for club and country simultaneously,” writes Bruce Mair. “He was player-manager of the Republic of Ireland, a part-time post, from May 1973 until March 1980 while playing for Leeds United (1973-75) and serving as player-manager of both West Bromwich Albion (1975-77) and Shamrock Rovers (1977-80). Giles selected himself for 24 of his 59 international appearances.”

Those are the most high-profile examples in Britain and Ireland, but there are dozens more cases – thanks to Bruce Mair, in particular, for doing so much work on this. We’ve picked some of the more interesting examples:

Andy Aitken “The earliest player-manager I can find,” writes Bruce. “Won three caps for Scotland while player-manager of Middlesbrough, 1907-08, and three more when player-manager/secretary at Leicester Fosse (now Leicester City), 1910-11.

Orvar Bergmark “Played 41 internationals for Sweden, including their run to the 1958 World Cup final, while player‑manager of Örebro between 1958 and 1961.”

Gunnar Gren “Seventeen caps for Sweden while player-manager of Örgryte IS, 1957-58. A teammate of Orvar Bergmark in the Swedish side that reached the 1958 World Cup final.”

Stuart Pearce “Capped twice for England in 1997 during his stint as caretaker player-manager at Nottingham Forest.”

Fanny Vágó “Hungary’s most‑capped women’s international made 19 appearances for her country while player‑manager of Ferencvárosi TC between 2021 and 2023.”

Elisha Scott “Liverpool legend won four caps for Northern Ireland while player-manager of Belfast Celtic at the tail end of his career, 1934-36.”

John Toshack “Six appearances for Wales as Swansea City player-manager in 1979.”

Jim Platt “Played twice for Northern Ireland in 1984 as player-manager of Ballymena United and made one further appearance as player-manager of Coleraine in 1986. Member of Northern Ireland’s 1986 World Cup squad.”

Knowledge archive

“Has there ever been an occasion where a major team has been disrupted by jury service, with either a manager or a player being called up during the season?” James Schofield asked back in May 2018.

“Plymouth’s Welsh international Carl Fletcher once tried to argue he couldn’t sit on a jury as he was too well known,” answered Andy Carswell. “According to reports in 2010, Judge Francis Gilbert told the midfielder that being Plymouth captain was not sufficient reason to excuse him, and that he had enough time to travel to Cheltenham for a Johnstone’s Paint Trophy tie after completing his duties. Fletcher argued that his position meant he was in a position of potentially being threatened, saying: ‘I don’t want anything to come back on me for sitting on a jury.’ His protests fell on deaf ears, with Judge Gilbert adding: ‘Lots of well-known people, some more famous than you, have been required to sit on juries.’”

James Perch had just helped Newcastle United to fifth place in 2012 but was also forced to cut short a holiday to Dubai after learning of his higher calling. “I’ve got jury service, unless I can be excused,” he told the club website. “It’s killed my holiday a bit, but at the minute I’m set to be in court at the end of May.”

Can you help?

“As someone who occasionally has to search for football stadiums to find directions and the like, I always enjoy that people take the time to rate their experience of visiting a football ground,” begins our own Will Unwin. “Hull City, for example, have 4.3 stars from 3,655 reviews. I therefore ponder … which ground has the highest and lowest Google rating?”

“I was surprised, staggered in fact, to see Nottingham Forest as the 18th team in the Guardian season previews,” writes Ross Connett. “I associate 18th place with the likes of Tottenham or West Ham, never a team beginning with N, just scraping over halfway into the alphabet. Has there ever been a more ‘early alphabet team’-dominated Premier League?”

“During Fulham v Chelsea, the previous jobs of both the opposing managers was coincidentally at the same club, Real Madrid,” notes Sarang Satish. “Are there other times this has happened?”

“Who has scored the highest percentage of their professional goals in hat-tricks?” asks Michael D.

“Last weekend every match in the Gibraltar league was a draw,” mails Stephen Hogg. “There are very few teams in the league, however. What’s the biggest league where this has happened?”

“This season Istanbul has six clubs in the Turkish top flight,” starts Vasco Wackrill. “What is the record number of top-flight clubs supplied in a season by a non-capital city?”

“Three of Kevin Lisbie’s sons are playing professionally; in the Championship (Kyrell, Millwall), in League One (Kyreece, Reading) and League Two (Kaion, Colchester United),” writes Stuart Willsher. “Have we ever had four brothers playing in all four top English divisions?”

Sports.title: Chelsea send email urging fans to bin sectarian chant sung during Fulham clash
Sports.content:
Chelsea have warned fans they could face an 'indefinite suspension' should they be found guilty of singing a sectarian chant.

In an email sent to supporters, the Blues hailed their 'passion and backing' during the 3-2 win over Fulham at Craven Cottage on Monday.



2 Chelsea fans were in fine voice on Stamford Bridge, although they have been reminded not to sing certain chants Credit: Getty

However, the club confirmed it received reports a 'small portion' of the travelling fans engaged in sectarian chanting.

Chelsea issue stern warning over sectarian chants

"We would like to strongly remind all supporters that the club does not condone any chants which discriminate against a protected characteristic," Chelsea wrote.

"Any supporter found guilty of this will face the strongest possible action, which could include indefinite suspension from attending all Chelsea matches and ejection from the stadium.



"Following previous club fines and charges for chants of this nature, and to ensure that we create a welcoming matchday experience for all, we ask supporters to take collective responsibility and remain vigilant in helping us to tackle discriminatory chanting."

Chelsea were fined over £8,000 in January 2025 for singing an anti-IRA chant during a 5-1 win over Shamrock Rovers in the Conference League.



How Chelsea's Premier League opener against Fulham unfolded

The Blues began Monday's contest against Fulham in brilliant fashion, with Joao Pedro putting the visitors in front within the opening minute.

However, Chelsea's lead lasted just over 20 minutes as Joshua King equalised.



It was a moment Blues goalkeeper Robert Sanchez would rather forget as he failed to make what appeared to be a simple save and instead dived too late.

Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea earlier this summer for a British record £117million, restored the visitors' lead just before half time before Cole Palmer doubled the advantage in the 49th minute.

Gonzalo Garcia pulled one back for the hosts five minutes later, but the Blues held on for all three points.

2 The Xabi Alonso era at Chelsea has got off to a brilliant start Credit: Getty



Speaking after the contest, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso believed the performance was the perfect platform to build from.

What did Xabi Alonso say about Chelsea's win over Fulham?

"It feels very good for sure, and you know how tough it is to win any Premier League game, any Premier League away game, but we were prepared for an intense game," Alonso said.

"I think it's been a very professional, solid performance, with maturity, matching different momentum during the game.

"We got the lead quite early, we had chances to score the second goal a few times, and after the equalise we went through ten minutes when we had not chosen the right [way] to press and the movement, but we have corrected well this, and in the second half we have felt comfortable without the ball controlling the game.



"I think it's a performance to build for the future, improve things for sure, but it's a good first day."

Alonso will look to make it two wins from two on Thursday when Chelsea host Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup, with kick-off scheduled for 7:30pm.

Sports.title: Aston Villa could sign on-strike EFL defender after move for £25m star hijacked by Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Aston Villa could sign on-strike EFL defender after move for £25m star hijacked by Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace have hijacked Aston Villa's move for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez, talkSPORT understands.

Palace have thrashed out a deal which will see Ordonez join on an initial loan with an obligation to buy in a deal totalling £25million.

4 Club Brugge defender Ordonez is set to join Crystal Palace despite talks with Aston Villa Credit: Getty

Ordonez has given the green light to move to Selhurst Park.

talkSPORT reported last week that Villa were closing in on the Club Brugge centre-back, with advanced talks ongoing.

But they have now been pipped to the post by their Premier League rivals, who are going to bring in the Ecuadorian instead.

Villa were hoping to sign Ordonez as a replacement for Ezri Konsa after he left the club to join Arsenal earlier this month.

Their pursuit came after having two bids rejected for £30m-rated Southampton star Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

However, Unai Emery is now going to either have to pay up for Harwood-Bellis or move on to a third centre-back target.

Unexpected target

Another potential alternative comes in the form of West Ham centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo, the Athletic reports.

The Frenchman is desperate to leave the Hammers, who are playing in the Championship as a result of their relegation last season.

talkSPORT understands Todibo is currently refusing to play for West Ham, such is his determination to secure a move away this summer.

Todibo, who has three years left on his contract, fell out with manager Nuno Espirito Santo after being hauled off in the first half of the Hammers’ defeat at Newcastle in the penultimate game of last season. He also fell out with one of his Nuno's predecessors in Julen Lopetegui.

4 Todibo joined West Ham from French club Nice in a £32.5m deal Credit: Getty

Crystal Palace's centre-back signings

Palace have swooped in to sign Ordonez before Aston Villa as they continue adding some new defenders to their squad.

Chris Richards, Jaydee Canvot and Chadi Riad started their Premier League opener against Everton on Saturday afternoon.

That line-up came after Maxence Lacroix left the club for Chelsea, with Riad then picking up an injury in the 2-0 defeat.

So, with them left short at the back, new manager Pierre Sage has had to act, already signing Axel Disasi on loan.

And now he's bringing in Ordonez to add further reinforcement and quality to his back line before the transfer deadline.

Oscar Mingueza and ex-Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu have also joined the club this summer.

4 Ordonez will join Palace to add further reinforcements to their defence Credit: Getty

Who is Joel Ordonez?

Ordonez is a 22-year-old Ecuador international who represented his country at the 2026 World Cup over the summer.

He has made 124 appearances for Club Brugge since joining the club from Independiente del Valle in 2022. Of those games, 22 have come in the Champions League.

Brugge won the Belgian top-flight title last season, with Ordonez featuring in 33 of their 40 games.

That was the second league success that Ordonez has had with the club, also winning the title in the 2023/24 campaign.

The Ecuadorian has not played any games this season so far though, having been sidelined through injury.

Sports.title: Fascist dictator’s relative makes debut for club in same stadium his great-grandfather opened 99 years ago
Sports.content:
Fascist dictator’s relative makes debut for club in same stadium his great-grandfather opened 99 years ago

Lazio handed a debut to the great-grandson of fascist dictator Benito Mussolini on Sunday.

Defender Romano Floriani Mussolini came off the bench in their Serie A opener against Bologna.



3 Lazio handed a first-team debut to Floriani Mussolini against Bologna on Sunday Credit: Getty

The 23-year-old replaced the injured Adam Marusic at right-back after just 19 minutes at the Stadio Renato Dell'Ara.

Despite being booked for unsporting behaviour just three minutes later, he completed the match as Lazio won 1-0 away from home.

It marked his first appearance for the club, who he joined aged 13 back in 2016.



Floriani's family connections to Italy's fascist past has at times threatened to overshadow his football career, though.

Mussolini's great-grandson makes debut

According to reports in Italy, Lazio fans chanted 'Duce' during his debut in reference to Benito Mussolini's role as the country's fascist dictator.



The club previously distanced themselves from a section of the fanbase in 2019 after a banner was unveiled honouring him.

Mussolini founded fascism in Italy before becoming Prime Minister in 1922.



He would remain the country's leader until he was overthrown in 1943 having allied with Nazi Germany in World War II.

Although he maintained his position as 'Duce of Fascism', he was ultimately executed by the Italian resistance in 1945.

A direct connection could be made between Mussolini and the venue for his great-grandson's Lazio debut.

3 Floriani Mussolini is the great-grandson of fascist dictator Benito Mussolini Credit: Getty



The match on Sunday was played at Bologna's Stadio Renato Dall'Ara, their home since 1927.

Mussolini was involved in both the construction and the opening of the venue 99 years ago.

He arrived on horseback to lay the first done whilst the ground was being built.

Meanwhile, a statue of him riding a horse was erected underneath the stadium's iconic arch.



The likeness was destroyed in 1943 after the city of Bologna was liberated from fascist rule.

Who is Romano Floriani Mussolini?

Over 80 years on from Mussolini's death, his great-grandson is now forging a career in football.

3 Mussolini laid the first stone at the Stadio Renato Dall'Ara, where a statue of the dictator was also once displayed Credit: Getty

The full-back joined Lazio's academy after beginning his youth career at city rival's Roma.



He has since had loan spells at Pescara, Juve Stabia and Cremonese, with his Lazio debut marking his 99th senior club appearance.

Floriani was a teammate of Jamie Vardy's at Cremonese last season, but was unable to help the club avoid relegation from Serie A.

His time at Juve Stabia was not without controversy, though, after it was alleged he celebrated a goal with a fascist salute.

The incident occurred after Floriani scored the winner in a victory over Cesena in December 2024.



Juve Stabia strongly denied the allegations in the Italian press at the time.

Sports.title: Man United forced into kit change after breaking little-known rule on opening day
Sports.content:
Manchester United broke Premier League kit rules during their opening fixture of the season and have been forced to make an amendment.

The Red Devils suffered a disappointing opening day defeat to newly promoted Hull City at the MKM Stadium last weekend.



3 Man United will be forced to wear the Premier League badge on both sleeves Credit: Getty

The 13-time Premier League winners went into the campaign without a sleeve sponsor following the end of their contract with DXC Technology.

It was a £20million pound a year deal which dates back to 2022.

However, Premier League rules dictate that clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms.

The club and the Premier League have refused to comment on the fact that Michael Carrick's men left one side completely empty.



Man United are expected to have the top-flight badge on both sleeves when they return to action against Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Commercial search

The Red Devils are still seeking a new shirt sleeve sponsor, having had one for the past eight seasons.



Interestingly, the DXC Technology branding made a brief appearance on the new 2026/27 home kit during the final two fixtures of the 2025/26 season.

However, that marked the final outing of the partnership, as the commercial contract officially expired at the conclusion of that campaign.



The club's official 2026/27 kit launch imagery and promo photoshoots all sported completely blank left sleeves.

Currently, the Old Trafford outfit have a primary front-of-shirt sponsor with mobile technology brand Snapdragon in a deal worth over £60million per year.

3 Carrick suffered only his third defeat in 21 matches last weekend Credit: Getty

Additionally, Betway holds a major £20 million-per-season training kit sponsorship.



Mauled by the Tigers

However, the sleeve sponsor error will be the least of United's worries following their loss to the Tigers.

After the final whistle, captain Bruno Fernandes said: "Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment."

Carrick said: "Yeah, some [of the game] was okay, obviously bits to improve on. It was never going to be perfect today but I think going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult, probably a typical one of those games of a newly promoted team at home.



"You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to, and then after that, we had moments, we had opportunities, we just didn't have that spark to then put the chances away or create any more.

3 Carrick will hope his team will be more prepared ahead of another fixture against a newly promoted side Credit: Getty

"Listen, we're bitterly disappointed with the result today but it won't knock us."

He added: "Inside, we are hurting. The boys know we need to get better.



"We've lost one game and it's a bad one to lose. But it won't change anything."

Sports.title: Everton star could leave in final week of window amid interest from Italy and Turkey
Sports.content:
Everton star could leave in final week of window amid interest from Italy and Turkey

Everton will listen to offers for Jake O'Brien in the final days of the transfer window, talkSPORT understands.

O'Brien is keen to leave the club after being forced to play at right-back for the Toffees for the last two seasons.



2 O'Brien could leave Everton before the transfer deadline on September 1 Credit: Getty

David Moyes has been playing the 25-year-old, who is naturally a centre-back, on the right of his back four.

But that seems to be part of the reason why he now wants to depart Goodison Park before the transfer deadline.

O'Brien admitted that he was okay playing in the make-shift position as long as he was starting when speaking in December.



However, he did say that he wanted to 'eventually go back to playing centre-back week-in, week-out' in the same interview.

And he could now make a move away from the club to try and find a team where he can do that in the final days of the window.



O'Brien wants Everton exit

O'Brien was an unused substitute for Everton in their opening game of the Premier League season against Crystal Palace.

And on a potential move away, talkSPORT's Senior Football Correspondent Ben Jacobs explained: "Everton are expected to listen to offers and this is a potential exit driven more by the player than the club.



"The Republic of Ireland international wants to start more regularly and, crucially, not be a make-shift right-back.

"Some footballers will say they'll play anywhere, but at his age, peak age, there's a real desire to move into that central defensive role, and I'm not so sure that Everton can guarantee him that particular position.

"You've got Jarrad Branthwaite, James Tarkowski as well... and the fact that O'Brien was an unused substitute in the opening victory over Crystal Palace shows you he needs to find another option if he wants to play every single week."

2 Moyes has played O'Brien at right-back in recent months, but that may lead to his exit Credit: PA



Who could Jake O'Brien sign for?

O'Brien has made 57 Premier League appearances for Everton and made 27 appearances in Ligue 1 during his stint with Lyon.

So, he boasts plenty of top-flight experience and Jacobs thinks he will have plenty of clubs looking at signing him.

"What I'm told is that there's some interest from Italy," he said.

"There have been some initial approaches from Turkey as well, and Crystal Palace took a look early in the window as well.

"So, he won't be short of options and it's fair to say that if he finds a move in the next few days, then Everton won't stand in his way."



Benfica are also understood to be a potential option for O'Brien, with the Portuguese giants aware that O'Brien is now available.

Sports.title: Wolves player who made just two Premier League starts backed to become main man
Sports.content:
Wolves player who made just two Premier League starts backed to become main man

Wolves attacker Fer Lopez has been backed to become one of the stars of the season after reigniting his career at the club.

The Spaniard has scored three goals in four appearances this season, which included a double in Saturday's 3-1 win at Preston North End.



3 Lopez claimed his loan spell back at Celta Vigo made him 'more prepared for football' Credit: Getty

The 22-year-old struggled to settle after arriving at Molineux last summer in a £19million deal from Celta Vigo.

He managed just two Premier League starts and only made seven other appearances from the bench at the start of last season.

Lopez - who failed to be on the winning side for any of his top-flight games with eight defeats and a draw - was loaned back to his former side for the second half of the 2025/26 campaign.



After scoring once in 17 LaLiga outings, the attacking midfielder returned to Wolves upon their relegation to the Championship.

Now, following his impressive start to the season, Hugh Woozencroft has asked whether Lopez can be one of the stars of the season.



Fer Lopez revival at Wolves

Speaking to former Cardiff City captain Sean Morrison on talkSPORT's EFL All Access podcast, he said: "Fer Lopez for Wolverhampton Wanderers, assist in game one, lovely solo goal in his brace this weekend as well.

"We're reflecting on other teams and kind of just that little impetus, that quality; he may have come a little bit from nowhere.



"He's obviously a £19m player playing in the second tier. Do you think he could go on to be one of the stars of this season?"

Morrison, a former League One Play-Offs Final winner with Huddersfield Town, replied: "Of course, yeah.

Abundance of quality in Fer Lopez

"As a player, if you carry a price tag of that amount of money, there is an abundance of quality in there," Morrison continued.

3 Lopez is quickly endearing himself to the Wolves faithful after a difficult first season Credit: Getty



"Somebody's seen something where they want to pay that amount of money for you.

"So we know the quality is there, and last season it didn't work out.

"Wolves were in a difficult position last year with a lot going on all around the club, whether that be on the pitch or off the pitch.

"So it would have been a turbulent place for him to come back to. Probably didn't settle as well as he would have wanted to.

"The club's a little bit more settled now. They've come down a division. Can he be the main man?



"Can the manager put his arm around him and give him the love that he probably wants and needs from his team and go on and have an absolutely brilliant season?

3 Lopez played just two minutes in his final Premier League appearance last December - a 1-1 draw with Manchester United Credit: Getty

"Wolves, for me, their squad is absolutely stacked with quality all over, especially at the top end of the pitch.

"I think they're going to be absolutely a fantastic team to watch this year. I think they're going to be goals by the dozen.



"So I think if you get him and the rest of those boys playing to the top end of their ability, they're going to be a real one to watch."

Woozencroft added: "Wolves will be feeling confident, and Nathan Shi, their chairman, has been speaking about the need to bring in more players.

"So it looks like they could add some more quality before the end of the window.

"They'll be looking around feeling very confident at the start of this campaign."

Sports.title: ‘Zero per cent chance’ – Atletico Madrid drop bombshell statement on Julian Alvarez amid Arsenal links
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have slammed claims Julian Alvarez is a 'victim' in his ongoing transfer saga.

The Spanish giants released a damning statement on Wednesday after Barcelona claimed they were still interested in signing the forward.

3 Atletico have issued a statement denying claims Alvarez is the 'victim' in his transfer saga Credit: Getty

Alvarez has expressed his desire to leave Atletico for the LaLiga champions this summer.

However, Barca had appeared to be out of the race to sign the 26-year-old before the transfer window closes.

Real Madrid have also had a bid rejected, whilst talkSPORT revealed at the weekend that Arsenal are actively exploring a deal.

Alvarez missed training due to illness on Wednesday as speculation surrounding his future continues.

Barcelona's Alvarez intentions

Atletico's statement followed comments made by Barcelona president Joan Laporta.

Speaking to the club's media channels, he explained: "Let them know that if they are willing to sell the player during this summer transfer window, we would be ready to buy him, provided we can reach an agreement regarding the offer we have made them."

Laporta went on to add: "We remain very interested in Julian Alvarez.

"We would like them to accept our offer and we are doing so with the utmost respect for Atletico Madrid. We would like to reach an agreement."

Atletico's £150million asking price this summer had appeared to rule Barca out of the race for Alvarez's signature.

The Argentina international has four years remaining on his contract after signing from Manchester City in 2024.

3 Laporta has revealed Barcelona remain interested in signing Alvarez this summer Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, manager Diego Simeone has previously revealed the club do not plan to sell Alvarez.

Atletico statement

In the wake of Laporta's remarks, Atletico issued a bombshell statement, per Marca.

The club said: "The player is being portrayed as a victim, but the only victims in the Julian case are us. They’ve hurt us financially and socially.

"There is a zero per cent chance of selling him to Barca. This situation isn’t about money, it’s about dignity.

"A campaign has been created with many lies and half-truths. The only one paying the price for this is Atletico."

Their stance comes days after Alvarez was booed by Atletico fans during his first appearance of the campaign.

3 Alvarez has expressed his desire to leave Atletico, who value the forward at £150million Credit: Getty

After being left out for their season opener, he appeared off the bench against Villarreal on Sunday.

The striker was loudly jeered as he made his way onto the pitch before being sent down the tunnel by the supporters at full time.

Latest on Arsenal's Alvarez interest

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has also provided an update on the Gunners' pursuit of Alvarez, revealing on The Window: "If the door even slightly opens to allow Arsenal to sign Julian Alvarez, they will move. And yet, this is all about what does the player want to do.

"Atleti want clarity. We know he wants Barcelona. Atleti have said publicly and privately they don’t want to sell to Barcelona.

"Alvarez didn’t train today. Reports in Spain say he has a stomach bug, but it’s a really tense situation between Atletico Madrid and Julian Alvarez.

"When Atleti came to London, and some reports said they were negotiating for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson, my understanding is that was a smoke screen.

"Actually, there were conversations between Arsenal and Atleti. So Arsenal have confidence late in this window.

"They could agree a package with Atletico Madrid, but it all just depends on the player."

Sports.title: National League chairman being ‘held hostage’ by star who has ‘downed tools’ after record bid
Sports.content:
National League chairman being ‘held hostage’ by star who has ‘downed tools’ after record bid

Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter has expressed his frustration about the Abdul Abdulmalik transfer saga.

The 23-year-old arrived at Meadow Park in the summer of 2024 following his release from Millwall, playing an instrumental role in their immediate return to the National League via the play-offs in his maiden campaign.

2 Abdulmalik is eyeing up the biggest move of his career Credit: Getty

He propelled his game to new heights last term as Boreham Wood were seconds away from reaching the Football League for the first time in their history.

Notching 15 goals and nine assists in the league including two strikes in their play-off campaign, Abdulmalik was at the heart of a record-breaking campaign which saw them clinch the National League Cup before losing to Rochdale on penalties in the play-off final at Wembley Stadium.

Such an impressive campaign has unsurprisingly attracted plenty of admirers, with Swedish side Djurgardens tabling two offers, with the most recent bid of £1.5million being rebuffed.

The deal would have broken the record for a National League transfer, exceeding the £1m Leicester City forked out for Jamie Vardy from Fleetwood Town in 2012.

Hunter, who took over the Hertfordshire-based outfit in 1999, has overseen much of Boreham Wood’s success since the turn of the millennium but now finds himself in the midst of a transfer saga.

The National League Young Player of the Season featured in their opening two matches of the season, scoring in a 3-1 victory at FC Halifax Town, before being left out of their squad against Forest Green Rovers on Saturday.

Speaking in his programme notes ahead of their clash against Boston United tomorrow, he appreciates Abdulmalik’s desire to seek pastures new, but feels his hand is being forced into accepting a fee below his true value.

“As such, my conscience is very clear, I’m sleeping well and I’m very happy regarding both my and our Club’s overall behaviour regarding all things Abdul-related,” the club Chairman explained.

“I, of course, understand the new agent, player, family and advisors are not happy, as they are only thinking about Abdul and themselves, but that is very much their concern.

“In our defence, we had made it very clear after our Wembley defeat to eight or nine of our players’ agents, who we knew might look to attract interest from other clubs, that as a club we had our own ambitions this season and we were not looking to sell certain players here at any price.

2 Boreham Wood chairman Hunter is standing his ground Credit: Getty

“I felt we were respectful and very open with every agent and every player, and I was crystal clear on our stance.

“I now feel I’m being made out to be the bad guy here and slightly held hostage, as it’s very late in the transfer window and I’m now forced into negotiating a transfer because the said player, on advice from others, has downed tools.

“At the moment, Abdul is refusing to train with us or play, though he is still very much our player and has two years left on his contract.

“Our valuation is set, it is fair and we will not be lowering it any more than the £350k that we already have over the next five days.”

Djurgardens, who are headed by ex-West Ham United recruitment chief Maximilian Hahn, have a track record of developing young stars, with Birmingham City's August Priske signing from the Stockholm-based side in January.

What has Abdulmalik said?

The forward addressed the situation on Tuesday and declared he was ready for a new challenge.

Biggest non-league transfer sales Jamie Vardy — £1,000,000 (Fleetwood Town to Leicester City, 2012) Shwan Jalal — £750,000 (Woking to Peterborough United, 2007) Jack Taylor — £500,000 (Barnet to Peterborough United, 2020) Richard Brodie — £275,000 (York City to Crawley Town, 2010) Jermaine Beckford — £225,000 (Wealdstone to Leeds United, 2006)

"Through sheer hard work and perseverance, the opportunity to progress has come around," Abdulmalik wrote.

"This is my chance to push myself as a footballer, elevate my game and most importantly fulfil my promise to the ones around me.

"Opportunities like this are rare, especially within the National League where some of the hardest working talent is overlooked. The game of football is forever changing and decisions are fast paced. There's no guarantee that the same chances come knocking twice.

"I owe it to myself and the kids growing up just like me to fight for this one I've been offered.

"Moving on from a club is one of the toughest decisions in a footballer's career. I'm more than grateful for everyone that has been a part of my journey so far.

"Everyone at Boreham Wood FC and the incredible fans have played a massive part. You will always have my respect.

"With this said, I'm ready for the next challenge. I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top."

Sports.title: Chelsea in talks over £36m-rated Atalanta teenager, Crystal Palace hijack Aston Villa's move for £25.7m Joel Ordonez - and Aston Villa expect Al-Hilal to pay £50m asking price for Ollie Watkins: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Villa ask West Ham about Konsa replacement Aston Villa have asked about West Ham defender Jean-Clair Todibo as they search for a centre back to replace Ezri Konsa. Villa look to be missing out on Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez who is heading to Crystal Palace while they have also had an offer rejected for Southampton's Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Todibo has also had interest from Italy and France in recent weeks. Honest teen heading to Chelsea Chelsea are progressing in talks with Atalanta over their 18-year-old defender Honest Ahanor. Already an Italy international, Ahanor can play at left-back and centre-back. Atalanta are asking for over £36million for the teenager but discussions are said to be positive. Chelsea are progressing in talks with Atalanta over their 18-year-old defender Honest Ahanor Palace hijack Villa's Ordonez move Crystal Palace have stepped in to hijack Aston Villa's move for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez. The 22-year-old is injured but expected to be fit by next month so will need to pass his medical. However, Palace have agreed a loan with obligation to buy the Ecuador international at £25.7m plus add ons and a sell-on clause. Crystal Palace have stepped in to hijack Aston Villa's move for Club Brugge defender Joel Ordonez Boro pip Birmingham to Split star Middlesbrough have fended off competition from Birmingham City to sign Hajduk Split midfielder Rokas Pukstas. Boro have agreed to pay his £4.2million buy out clause and the player is due to travel for his medical after playing in the Europa Conference League tomorrow. The 21-year-old, who had a trial with Manchester United as a teenager, was born in Oklahoma, USA and started out with Sporting Kansas City before moving to Barcelona's academy where he was spotted by Split. His father, Mindaugas Pukstas, represented Lithuania at the 2004 Olympics in the marathon. Pukstas Jr, who has represented USA at U23 level, was watched by several scouts last Thursday as Split drew 2-2 in their Conference League qualifying first leg against Rakow Czestochowa. A condition of the deal is that he is allowed to play for Split in the return game tomorrow night. Birmingham also held talks with the midfielder but he was more convinced by Boro's project. Sunderland submit loan for Grealish Sunderland have submitted a bid to take Jack Grealish on loan from Manchester City. All options remain open to the 30-year-old, who has featured as a substitute in City's first two games of the season. United's Overy joining Sydney Manchester United youngster James Overy is joining Sydney FC. The 18-year-old right-back was born in Perth and is an Australia international. His United team-mate Louis Jackson is in talks to join St Mirren. The 20-year-old defender is due to have a medical tomorrow. Both deals will include sell-on and buy-back clauses. Schlotterbeck to be made a Saint Southampton have agreed a £3.8million deal with Augsburg for defender Keven Schlotterbeck. The 29-year old centre-back is undergoing a medical this afternoon. Keven Schlotterbeck is set for sign for Southampton Louza's a winner for Panathinaikos Panathinaikos have agreed a deal to sign Watford midfielder Imran Louza. The fee for the 27-year-old Morocco international is worth £6.8m. Louza has travelled to Athens ahead of joining the Greek club. Derby set to welcome Meister Derby County are closing on Pisa striker Henrik Meister. The initial deal is a loan with an option to buy for £7.2m but the overall cost will be £8.5m if Meister joins Derby permanently. Kabore completes Wrexham medical Manchester City right-back Issa Kabore has completed a medical ahead of his £2m move to Wrexham. The Burkina Faso international has agreed a three-year deal. Wrexham are also adding Angers left-back Jacques Ekomie who has completed a medical ahead of his £8m move. Martinez offered to Chelsea Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their wantaway goalkeeper. After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park. For more on this story click HERE Emiliano Martinez reached the World Cup final with Argentina in the summer Liverpool check on Palace's Sarr Liverpool have checked on a deal for Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr, though any move looks unlikely as it stands. The Anfield club have been assessing different opportunities in the market as they look to add two attacking players before Tuesday. They have not made an offer for Sarr as it stands. For more on this story click HERE Sunderland in for Brazilian winger Igor Sunderland are in talks with Marseille for Brazilian winger Igor Paixao. Leeds have previously checked on 26-year-old Paixao. Sunderland are understood to have made an offer earlier this week and talks are continuing. Marseille need to raise funds and Sunderland's priority is to add a winger. They have also been in talks with Sporting Lisbon over Mozambique winger Geny Catamo. Bees agree Malick Diouf deal Brentford have agreed a deal with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf worth £35m plus add-ons. Daily Mail Sport reported Brentford's interest last month and the clubs have now come to an agreement. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season. Brentford have agreed a deal for El Hadji Malick Diouf of West Ham Disasi in at Palace Crystal Palace have announced the arrival of Axel Disasi on a straight loan from Chelsea. The 28-year-old centre-back replaces Maxence Lacroix, who went the other way in a £52million move earlier in the window. Disasi provides experience in the centre of Palace’s back three, with the Frenchman expected to play in the middle of Chris Richards and Jaydee Canvot. Palace remain in the market for another centre-back following Chadi Riad’s injury during last weekend’s 2-0 defeat to Everton. BOBBY MANZI Brighton's £3.5m Orozco deal Brighton are working on a £3.5million deal to sign 18-year-old midfielder Matias Orozco from Colombian side Deportivo Cali. Orozco, a defensive midfielder, has been watched by Liverpool and Manchester United among others. He is due in the UK to complete formalities of the transfer and is expected be sent out on loan initially. Man City complete ins and outs as they wait to go back in for Enzo Manchester City's Omar Marmoush will sign a contract at Tottenham tomorrow after having his medical today, while Nico Gonzalez is finalising his move to Newcastle with the second part of his medical. City are signing Palmeiras winger Allan Elias - who will fly in from Brazil to complete his move tomorrow - while a City bid is expected to go in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. City have confirmed the £85.6m signing of 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille. The Morocco midfielder said: 'Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. 'It’s a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player. I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game. 'I’ve watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football and they have shown they are winners – this club feels like it’s built to win. The squad is world class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager.' Ayyoub Bouaddi has joined Manchester City in a £85.6m deal from Lille Aston Villa expect Saudis to meet £50m Watkins asking price Aston Villa expect Al Hilal to hit their valuation of £50million for Ollie Watkins if they complete a deal for the England forward. Watkins is keen to move to the Saudi Pro League club, who are offering a salary far higher than his current wages at Villa. Villa have so far stuck to their position on Watkins and there is growing optimism Al Hilal, who have already had four bids turned down, will eventually meet the asking price. Villa are also pursuing the £65million signing of Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea, who would effectively replace Watkins. TOM COLLOMOSSE Monaco join queue for Spurs star Matar Sarr Monaco have joined the list of clubs showing interest in signing Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr. Monaco are looking at the market for new midfielders in case they lose Lamine Camara who has attracted offers from Crystal Palace and interest from Chelsea. All options open for Grealish as clock ticks down Manchester City are leaving all options open to Jack Grealish as the window draws to a close. The 30-year-old has returned to City's first-team fold, appearing as substitute in their first two games. He was on loan at Everton last season and their chief executive Angus Kinnear says they have remained in contact. City have not ruled out a permanent sale. Nor have they ruled out another loan or an option to stay, though that could be with potentially limited game time. Coach Enzo Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's win over Bournemouth: 'He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best. 'Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players.' Jack Grealish is now back at Manchester City but all options are open as the window closes Liverpool look elsewhere with Minteh fee too high Liverpool are exploring alternative wing options with Brighton's valuation of Yankuba Minteh considered too high. As Daily Mail Sport reported at the weekend, Brighton have been looking for a figure closer to £80million for the 22-year-old Gambian who is out until October with injury. Liverpool had initially hoped to strike a deal around £50m. Meanwhile, Celta Vigo are understood to be interested in midfielder Stefan Bajcetic but Liverpool have yet to receive a formal approach. The 21-year-old started out at Vigo. Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024. Tottenham have asked about Forest full-back Neco Williams but he is expected to stay at the City Ground. As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Forest are also in talks over a £13.6m move including add ons for Corinthians midfielder Andre. The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but Corinthians are holding out for more. The 27-year-old has agreed a four-year contract. As Daily Mail Sport reported yesterday, Ipswich want £9m for midfielder Anis Mehmeti, who has offers from Wrexham, Birmingham and Derby. Ezequiel Palacios is set to became the latest signing in a busy summer at Portman Road Osmajic leaves Preston Preston striker Milutin Osmajic has signed for Genoa. Deepdale boss Paul Heckingbottom confirmed the move was on the cards at the weekend and added to BBC Radio Lancashire: 'The business we've done so far has been really good in terms of players we've brought in to replace, players who have gone out, but we've lost a lot of players. We've still got a lot to replace and now Milly is another one we've got to replace.' Sports.title: Chelsea offered Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa - who Juventus bid just £6m for - to fix their goalkeeper problem after Robert Sanchez shocker
Sports.content:
Chelsea offered Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa - who Juventus bid just £6m for - to fix their goalkeeper problem after Robert Sanchez shocker

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Emiliano Martinez has been offered to Chelsea as Aston Villa seek a new club for their want-away goalkeeper.

After his move to Juventus collapsed earlier this month despite an initial £6million offer, Martinez is now one of three senior keepers in the Villa squad following the arrival of Zion Suzuki at Villa Park.

Martinez is also Villa's top earner following the departure of Youri Tielemans to Manchester United in July, and Unai Emery intends to press ahead with Suzuki and Marco Bizot.

Earlier in the summer, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated he was happy with keepers Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders.

But Sanchez's shaky display in Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham raised more question marks about the Spaniard.

Aston Villa have replaced Emiliano Martinez with Zion Suzuki and he is available for transfer

Asked about Sanchez on Wednesday, Alonso said: 'Normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context.

'Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related.'

Chelsea have brought 21-year-old Belgian Mike Penders into their squad after a successful loan at Strasbourg last season.

Alonso today suggested he is likely to start Thursday's Carabao Cup game against Luton Town. 'He's in the squad and will have an opportunity,' he said.

The Blues rate the former Genk youth shot-stopper, who has been likened to former Chelsea man Thibaut Courtois, very highly.

A move for Martinez, at 33 years old, would not be viewed as blocking Penders' progress.

The Argentina goalkeeper has been training with Villa since returning from the World Cup and his club say he is not injured.

Robert Sanchez's position as Chelsea No 1 is under threat after his recent errors

Emery confirmed he has once again asked to leave.

'We have signed Suzuki not for the future, but for now,' the Villa boss said. 'He has shown his capacity and that he can play at our level.

'Martinez transmitted to us the possibility to have another challenge in his career, not just now and even last year, and he was thinking in case he had a possibility to change his challenges, but he stayed and performed fantastic.

'This year, again, he transmitted to us for a new challenge, and we signed Suzuki to replace him. But the scenario we have is that we have two great goalkeepers.

'(Marco) Bizot as well, when we needed him, he responded fantastically. My ideal scenario with the goalkeeper is really fantastic, but maybe we can still change something.'

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes names the Man United starlet he coached while completing his badges... and reveals why he can't stand English tea!
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has revealed Manchester United team-mate Shea Lacey was under his tutelage when he was completing his coaching badges. Fernandes did his UEFA B diploma through United, along with Juan Mata and Nemanja Matic, and said he coached United starlet Lacey when the now 19-year-old was in the club's Under-14 side. 'His technical ability was never in doubt,' Fernandes told the Men in Blazers Media Network. 'I often joke with him because I coached him when I was taking my coaching badges, and I remember he was in the U14 team then. 'So, Juan Mata and I basically coached him for a day. I told him he's much better now than he was at 14. He is much more mature, doing very well. 'I think what they all need they want to be part of the team and play for the team is to treat every training session like a game.' Bruno Fernandes has revealed he coached Shea Lacey when he was doing his badges Lacey made his debut for the United first team against Aston Villa in December and was a second-half substitute in the shock 2-0 defeat by Hull on Saturday. He has been widely tipped for success at Old Trafford and captain Fernandes believes the team have already seen a different player compared to the star who broke through last season. 'I think Shea Lacey came with a completely different mentality this season in terms of movement off the ball,' added Fernandes. 'I think that's great, and it's what I talked to him about after returning from vacation, because I watched their three games. He plays in the same position as me, which requires a high level of running and emotional intelligence in covering space and assisting teammates in attack, and he has done very well.' Fernandes was this week crowned PFA Player of the Year after a stellar campaign at Old Trafford, which included breaking the Premier League assists record. The 31-year-old has spent six and a half years in England after moving to United from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020. Asked whether there was anything Mancunian about him now, he said: 'I would say not much. 'The only thing is that I now really like going to coffee shops. To be honest, I used to go in Portugal, but only for breakfast. Now, at any time of day, I can go for a coffee, which I wasn't used to doing. The Man United captain was speaking in an interview on the Men in Blazers Media Network 'I still don't drink English black tea; I can't mix water with milk, sorry, and then tea. That's not for me yet. But Tom Heaton always has a cup of tea in his hand at any time of day. But if he calls me for a coffee I will always go. Maybe not tea, maybe a cappuccino, maybe another kind, like a latte, I don't know, but not English tea yet!' United will aim to bounce back from the loss at Hull when they face another newly-promoted team in Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday. Fernandes fumed at his team-mates after the 2-0 reverse at the MKM Stadium, blasting the side for making the 'same mistakes as last season'. The comments prompted ex-United midfielder Paul Scholes to tell the Portuguese midfielder he 'needs to keep his mouth shut'.

Sports.title: Man United's kit clanger: Club's opening game shirt falls foul of Premier League laws as Red Devils are reminded of little-known rule after Hull City defeat
Sports.content:
Man United's kit clanger: Club's opening game shirt falls foul of Premier League laws as Red Devils are reminded of little-known rule after Hull City defeat

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have fallen foul of Premier League kit rules after one game of the season.

The Old Trafford outfit went into the current campaign without a sleeve sponsor, following the expiration of a £20m per year deal with DXC Technology which dates back to 2022.

However, Premier League rules dictate that clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms.

And eagle-eyed observers have pointed out that United did not comply during their opening day defeat at Hull City, with one sleeve left blank.

While both the Premier League and United declined to comment, Daily Mail Sport understands that the club was given a polite reminder of the rule.

Premier League rules dictate clubs without a sleeve sponsor should display the competition’s badge on both arms - but Manchester United did not

The Premier League badge was shown on the other arm of United's shirts

It is also understood that the top-flight badge will be on both sleeves when United return to action against Ipswich at Old Trafford on Sunday.

United are seeking a new shirt sleeve sponsor, having had one for the past eight seasons.

The rule-break came on a chaotic opening day for United and manager Michael Carrick, with the surprise defeat by Hull drawing plenty of criticism - including from captain Bruno Fernandes.

After the match, the United captain complained to the media that his side had made the 'same mistakes as we did last season (in away matches)'. The Portugal midfielder added: 'Every away game we give too much of the ball to them. In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

'We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.'

Club legend Paul Scholes, however, took issue with Fernandes' comments on his podcast The Good, The Bad & The Football.

'I'd be interested to know what he means by them. What mistakes were they giving away?' the 51-year-old former player said.

'Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut. He didn't have his best performance either.'

Scholes and former United forward Dion Dublin went further, suggesting that Fernandes, alongside team-mate Luke Shaw, who also claimed after the match that United went into the fixture underprepared, had undermined manager Michael Carrick.

Bruno Fernandes - pictured without the Premier League logo - was left disappointed

Shaw had said after the match: 'It’s not us and we knew it was coming. I think as a whole, as a group, collectively, we could prepare better. Especially knowing how good they are at set plays and what their dangers are.'

Reacting to the left-back's comments, Scholes said: 'Luke Shaw always says something. And that's a slight on your staff. That's a slight on your manager. If one of your players is saying that you'd be like f***ing hell, you'd have them in on Monday morning.'

Dublin said: 'You want silence. If your skipper has to speak then he has to speak, but then you make sure he says the things that don't open a can of worms. You just don't give anyone any ammunition because the ammunition is there from your performance.'

Scholes added: 'Those comments are not so much about respect but you speak about fear of managers and the things they've said, they're a slight on the manager and staff. As a player if we did that about Sir Alex, "we weren't prepared", f***ing hell, you'd be right in and he'd probably single you out in front of the full team.'

Sports.title: PGA Tour golfer handed six-month ban after getting caught gambling on tournaments
Sports.content:
PGA Tour golfer handed six-month ban after getting caught gambling on tournaments

Golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended by the PGA Tour for violating its integrity program, the organization announced on Wednesday.

Gogel, 55, was handed a six-month ban from any PGA Tour-sanctioned event after being found to have gambled on tournaments.

While the professional did not place bets on any event he was competing in, the gambling on PGA Tour competitions violates the Tour's policy.

Gogel competes on the PGA Tour Champions, the PGA Tour-sanctioned senior tour open to golfers age 50 and over.

He will now be unable to compete in any tournament sanctioned by the PGA Tour until February 22, 2027.

Gogel, who said he 'unknowingly' violated Tour policy with his gambling, cooperated fully throughout the process, the PGA Tour stated.

Golfer Matt Gogel has been suspended by the PGA Tour for violating its integrity program

The 55-year-old was handed a six-month ban from any PGA Tour-sanctioned event

'In 2024 and 2025, I unknowingly violated the PGA TOUR policy by placing small recreational wagers on golf,' Gogel said in a statement.

'I want to be clear that these wagers were not placed on regular PGA TOUR events, PGA TOUR Champions events or any tournament in which I participated.

'I would never knowingly violate the integrity of the game of golf. I made an honest mistake and I look forward to playing in 2027 on the PGA TOUR Champions.'

Gogel has competed in 18 events on the Champions Tour in 2026, earning prize money of more than $760,000.

He currently stands 20th in the Tour's season-long Charles Schwab Cup points race, which culminates with the Charles Schwab Cup Championship on November 12-15.

His ban came into effect on Sunday, the day on which Gogel finished tied 30th in the Rogers Charity Classic on the senior circuit.

The player was found to have placed bets on PGA Tour-sanctioned tournaments

The PGA Tour Integrity Program prohibits wagering on any Tour-sanctioned event around the world by members, but also by anyone in their immediate circle who receives credentials to tournaments, including family, caddies and agents.

'Any Covered Person, directly or indirectly, Betting on the outcome or any other aspect of any PGA TOUR Event, any other professional golf competition or any elite amateur golf competition (including Olympic Golf) anywhere in the world ('Professional Golf Event'),' the tour's rules state.

The manual defines 'betting' as '(A) placing any money or other thing of value on the occurrence of an uncertain outcome with the expectation of return or (B) participating in any fantasy or other game that awards a prize of value, including any free-to-play, paid or daily fantasy game, unless expressly approved by the PGA TOUR.'

Penalties range from mandatory education to fines up to $500,000, suspension to lifetime bans.

Sports.title: Sunderland submit loan offer for Jack Grealish: Man City considering options after 30-year-old's return to first-team fold
Sports.content:
Sunderland have submitted an offer to take Jack Grealish on loan. The 30-year-old has returned to City's first-team fold, appearing as substitute in their first two games, and the club are leaving all options open to him as the window draws to a close. It is understood Sunderland's bid includes covering part of the 30-year-old's salary. He was on loan at Everton last season and their chief executive Angus Kinnear says they have remained in contact. City have not ruled out a permanent sale, nor have they ruled out another loan or an option to stay, though that could be with potentially limited game time. Coach Enzo Maresca has not ruled out a move either, saying after Sunday's win over Bournemouth: 'He is here and it is my duty to coach Jack and to try to get the best. Sunderland have made an offer to sign Manchester City star Jack Grealish on loan 'Then it is one more week to go and we will see what happens. Not only with Jack but also other players.' City's Omar Marmoush is having his medical at Tottenham today and Nico Gonzalez is finalising his move to Newcastle. City are signing Palmeiras winger Allan Elias while a City bid is expected to go in for Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez. Sunderland manager Regis Le Bris sees winger as a position of importance and the club have also been in talks with Marseille for Brazilian winger Igor Paixao. Leeds have previously checked on 26-year-old Paixao. Sunderland are understood to have made an offer earlier this week and talks are continuing. They have also been in talks with Sporting Lisbon over Mozambique winger Geny Catamo.

Sports.title: KATIE McCABE interview: Why I made the move that rocked women's football, the social media backlash after joining Chelsea from Arsenal and why I can't wait to win trophies at Stamford Bridge
Sports.content:
KATIE McCABE interview: Why I made the move that rocked women's football, the social media backlash after joining Chelsea from Arsenal and why I can't wait to win trophies at Stamford Bridge

Of all the transfers that rocked the women's football world this summer, none were quite as dramatic as that of Katie McCabe's. Even with two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and former Lioness goalkeeper Mary Earps WSL bound, McCabe's move across the capital from Arsenal to Chelsea eclipsed them all.

McCabe had luckily anticipated the furore, making the prescient decision to take herself off social media while it was being announced. As a result, she managed to avoid the areas of the internet which made for grim viewing as incensed keyboard warriors reacted to the news, although she is, of course, keenly aware of it.

Now, just over a couple of months later, it is easy to understand why when McCabe takes a seat with Daily Mail Sport at Chelsea's Cobham training ground to talk about her decision to move from the club where she spent over a decade to their fiercest rivals, she is choosing her words carefully.

'Coming into the end of my Arsenal contract, there was a lot going on behind the scenes,' she says. 'It was important for me to connect with the people I trust and the people around me who care about me and know me – I was leaning on people for their support.

'And then having conversations with the Chelsea manager and understanding what she wanted and the clear ambitions from the club, it matched what I wanted perfectly. I'm just delighted to get going now.'

Arsenal's releasing of cult hero McCabe at the end of her contract this summer was a result of a longer-term strategy intended to freshen up the women's senior squad and bring the average age down. The 30-year-old has joined long-serving players such as Beth Mead, 31, and goalkeeper Manuela Zinsberger, 30, out of the door.

Even with two-time Ballon d'Or winner Putellas and former Lioness goalkeeper Earps WSL bound, McCabe's move across the capital from Arsenal to Chelsea eclipsed them all

Record eight-time WSL winners Chelsea managed to bat off competition from last season's champions Manchester City for the left back's signature this summer

The fact the club decided to offer McCabe a new contract in April, as per reports, suggests they realised they had made a mistake. But by then it was too late. The wheels were in motion, and record eight-time WSL winners Chelsea managed to bat off competition from last season's champions Manchester City for the left back's signature.

Yet the intricacies of a football transfer, where countless conversations are happening behind the scenes, are often lost on the masses ('You can't expect everyone to understand,' McCabe graciously says).

In this instance, the vitriol was uncomfortable. Among them, one person shared a picture on X of a cut-up McCabe jersey. Another, who labelled her a 'snake', wrote: 'This is probably the worst thing Katie McCabe could have done for not only her career but as a person. You not only are hated by the Chelsea fans, but now you lose the support from the Arsenal fans who saw you as a legend.'

McCabe clearly anticipated that the fans of the club she has been loyal to for over 10 years would be surprised, but it's posed to her whether she foresaw this level of backlash.

'I think growing up the last 10, 11 years as an Arsenal player, being on that journey with the fans from Boreham Wood to what we had created to the Emirates, winning trophies together, it was always going to be difficult for the Arsenal fans to see me move on, especially to a rival club,' she says.

'I understand the frustrations and that, but coming off social media was more so the timing of everything. It was the first day of international camp that it got announced, and my focus was being away with Ireland. I didn't want anything to interfere with that, any outside noise.'

Social media abuse in the women's game is rife, with female athletes facing 19 per cent more online harassment than their male counterparts. It is a problem and unfortunately doesn't appear to be going away any time soon.

'I think if you're talking strictly football opinions, I'm all for that,' McCabe says. 'If people or pages tend to get personal, then that's another story.

Arsenal's releasing of McCabe at the end of her contract was a result of a longer-term strategy intended to freshen up the women's senior squad and bring the average age down

McCabe was lucky to avoid a third career red card in April when she pulled her new team-mate Alyssa Thompson's hair in a Champions League meeting with her new side

'I keep it at a distance. For me, the most important thing is what my team-mates think, the manager, staff and the people I work with around me and, of course, my close circle of people away from football. That comes with experience.'

Experience is something McCabe has in abundance. She may be one of the most successful women's players of the modern era, with seven major trophies in her cabinet, yet to the Arsenal team and its fanbase she was so, so much more. 'We've got McCabe', they would sing every matchday, which she happily echoed back to them after ending their decade-long wait for a Women's Champions League title.

McCabe is the type of player that you would love to have on your team but hate to play against. She is often viewed as the equal of Roy Keane, a useful comparison given she also wears the Ireland armband. Unlike Keane, McCabe has a surprisingly low red card count, just two in her career.

She was lucky to avoid a third in April when she pulled her new team-mate Alyssa Thompson's hair in a Champions League meeting with her new side. The incident, which she claimed was a mistake, saw her new manager Sonia Bompastor receive her marching orders.

And while much has been made of those childhood allegiances with Chelsea, the reality of McCabe's switch is far less sentimental. Chelsea signed her because they believe she can help them return to the top of the WSL and has experience of winning the one title that eludes them, the illustrious Champions League.

For McCabe, Arsenal may have been wanting younger blood, but she still feels like there's plenty left in the tank and didn't want to drop a level from one of the best clubs in England.

'I'm in a good space in my career,' she says. 'I feel good, I feel fit, and I still feel like I've got a lot to give, and I think that was part of my thought process. Chelsea are a team that have fundamentally won for the last how many seasons. I want to be part of that. I want to bring trophies to Stamford Bridge, and I know there's a hungry dressing room full of players as well that want that too.'

A player who likes to lead by example, McCabe makes it clear that she has no intention of barging into the place and immediately asserting herself, despite her leadership experience.

A player who likes to lead by example, McCabe makes it clear that she has no intention of barging into the place and immediately asserting herself, despite her leadership experience

'It's a new dressing room. It's a new environment. It's a new game model, so for me, it's about coming in, getting my head down, getting to work and earning the respect of my team-mates first and foremost.

'I've been working really closely with the team over the last few weeks, and with Sonia and the technical staff as well, to understand how we play. Then I can step into my role, bring my experience where I can and help the players around me too.

'There's two ways of looking at it, but for me, since I've come in, I just want to get my head down, work hard and show the girls I'm ready to be here and compete.'

McCabe won't have long until Chelsea host her old side at Stamford Bridge – they are just the third fixture to follow Aston Villa for next weekend's WSL opener. We await the home end singing 'We've got McCabe' with glee.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal £50m agreement, Man Utd land huge boost, Liverpool bid
Sports.content:
Ayyoub Bouaddi completes Man City transfer

Ayyoub Bouaddi has wasted no time in sticking the boot into his new rivals - after admitting Manchester City are the best club in the world.

The Moroccan sensation has completed an £85m switch to City from Lille.

The teenage midfielder has agreed a deal that will keep him at the Etihad until at least 2031.

And Bouaddi has told the likes of Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United there is no place he would rather be.

Bouaddi said: "Manchester City are, for me, the best club in the world. It's a dream to be here and be able to call myself a City player.

"I have spent most of my life working hard to become the best player I can be and reach the top of the game.

"I've watched City for many years, and I love their style of play. City always try and play quality football.

"And they have shown they are winners - this club feels like it's built to win.

"The squad is world-class and Enzo (Maresca) is a top manager. And I’m really looking forward to playing at the Etihad Stadium, in front of all the fans.

"I have plenty of improving to do. I am only 18. I am happy with the progress I have made so far, but I also know I can improve so much. This is undoubtedly the best place for me to do that.

"This club demands trophies and I will give everything to make sure we are challenging for every title."
