While those close to the negotiations have told Daily Mail Sport that the blockbuster bout is done, with New York’s Madison Square Garden understood to have been agreed as the venue, Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn has insisted there is still work to be done on the deal.

Those familiar with the discussions say Joshua and his promoter Hearn continued to push for the fight to take place in the UK, with Fury also keen on a homecoming bout, but they were ultimately unable to secure their preferred location.

However, Hearn - who recently revealed it was written into Joshua's contract that the fight has to be staged in Britain - has told Daily Mail Sport that no agreement has yet been reached to change those terms.

'We are in constant communication with Turki (Alalshikh, Saudi boxing supremo) and (Saudi Arabian sports company) SELA but as of yet there is no agreement to any variation within the contract,' he said.

It is understood that Anthony Joshua (left) and Tyson Fury (right) have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City

The fight is said to be taking in New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - where Joshua previously suffered his shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019

Turki Alalshikh (above), who is helping bankroll the fight, had left the door open to staging the event in Britain, but made it clear that the numbers had to work

Speaking in an interview released after Daily Mail Sport's story broke, Hearn added: "It seems like everyone is adamant the fight takes place in New York. There isn't really any consideration or willingness to speak to the government. Sadiq Khan, Transport for London. It's just like 'we want to do this fight in America'.

'Tyson Fury has agreed to do it in America and we haven't at the moment. We are talking through a roadmap of what that might look like to change the deal and if they do all the things we've discussed and agreed in principle, then I think there is a very good chance the fight will happen in America."

Others close to the discussions say Alalshikh's position was that the fight could be staged in the UK if the financial case stacked up and the figures could be demonstrated.

But with that case ultimately unable to be made, the decision has been taken to move the blockbuster to New York and the iconic Madison Square Garden - the scene of Joshua's shock defeat by Andy Ruiz Jr in June 2019.

The fight is expected to take place on a Friday night in an attempt to avoid clashes with major American sporting events and maximise its exposure in the US.

It remains unclear, however, whether the main event will take place at a time convenient for British boxing fans.

And while Hearn's comments indicate that the contractual position has yet to be formally altered, Daily Mail Sport understands the final pieces are now being put in place for the official announcement, with the relevant parties due to meet in the coming days to organise the launch press conference.

That is expected to take place before the end of August.

Anthony Joshua has his hand raised following victory over Kristian Prenga on July 25

However, result didn't come without drama as he was knocked down in the first 20 seconds

Spencer Brown, Fury's manager, said several weeks ago that the announcement would be made at an iconic British landmark, adding that it would be 'like no announcement' fans have ever seen before and claiming they 'don't want to miss it'.

Hearn has also previously told Daily Mail Sport that the announcement press conference would take place before the end of the month and would be timed around Joshua's return from holiday.

The roots of Joshua-Fury go back to the beginning of the 2010s, when both men were establishing themselves as Britain's leading heavyweight prospects.

Joshua won Olympic gold at London 2012 before turning professional, while Fury had already made his professional debut in 2008 and was building an unbeaten record of his own.

For years, the prospect of the two eventually meeting was one of British boxing's biggest talking points.

Fury's victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015 transformed him into a world heavyweight champion, while Joshua was rapidly moving towards the same position.

Joshua won the IBF heavyweight title by beating Charles Martin in 2016 and subsequently added the WBA and IBO belts.

By 2017, the possibility of an undisputed Joshua-Fury fight had become a genuine objective rather than simply a dream matchup.

Fury took on Mariusz Wach at the Max Muay Thai Stadium, Pattaya, Thailand on July 24

But the negotiations repeatedly failed.

The biggest opportunity came in 2021, when Joshua and Fury appeared to be moving towards a two-fight agreement. A deal was publicly discussed, but the proposed fight ultimately collapsed after Fury became obligated to face Deontay Wilder following an arbitration ruling.

Fury subsequently fought Wilder for a third time, while Joshua moved towards his own defining bouts.

Joshua then suffered back-to-back defeats against Oleksandr Usyk, losing his WBA, IBF and WBO titles in 2021 before being beaten again in their 2022 rematch.

The sport then appeared to get another opportunity to make Joshua-Fury. In late 2022, negotiations accelerated dramatically, with both camps discussing a proposed fight in December.

A deal again failed to materialise.

Fury instead moved on to other opponents, while Joshua continued his rebuilding process following the Usyk defeats.

The arrival of Alalshikh and the expansion of major boxing events in Saudi Arabia created a new route to making the fight.

Fury emerged victorious and had been expected ringside for AJ's fight with Prenga

Now, after years of failed negotiations and multiple points at which the fight appeared close before falling apart, the contracts have finally been signed.

Joshua-Fury is no longer a fight being negotiated.

It is happening.

November 20. Madison Square Garden. Or, so they say...

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua should not be fighting in New York - their fans have been forgotten and will now have to shell out their last pennies to see their heroes: JEFF POWELL
Sports.content:
For our next trick, how about the FA Cup final at Giants Stadium? Soulless. Never mind.

Then the Wimbledon finals on the good old hard courts of Flushing Meadows?

The Open? What holes in golf could be more challenging than the First to Eighteenth Streets in Manhattan? No soft landings there.

What about The Ashes? Where better for the Poms and the Okkers to dispute the Ashes than Yankee Stadium?

I could go on.

The selection of New York's Madison Square Garden for the longest awaited boxing match in UK ring history was not exactly a surprise. Wembley Stadium had given up on the Gypsy King v AJ weeks ago.

Where better for the last hurrah for two grand old British warhorses than Madison Square Garden? Even if that nostalgic mausoleum is not exactly the most sentimental last resting place for two lions of our own.

We sell our history at our peril.

But for Nett-Profit-Flix? And to the oil-mongers?

I am all for the men in gloves who put their lives on the line between the ropes making the most money they can for themselves and the generational future of their families.

But neither Tyson Fury nor Anthony Joshua are short of a few bucks and the fans who made them are forgotten in this sell-out. Even if they manage to prop open their eyelids with matchsticks into the early hours of a dank winter morning.

Many of the faithful will do so. Especially those who have been imploring Joshua and Fury to get it on for a couple of decades.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua look set to finally battle it out on November 20

Madison Square Garden in New York City is expected to host the heavyweight bout

The sad part, even though we will all be drawn to it like curious cats, is that they have missed their moment in time

No world title on the line. Historically beyond its time.

Delayed by all those involved in case one heavyweight or the other got knocked off his perch of public admiration and corporate income before they fought each other.

That obsession was exposed as nonsense by Oleksandr Usyk and Daniel Dubois.

So overpowering is the scent of nostalgia in this most compelling of sports that we still want to see what happens when two of our national heroes collide.

Hundreds if not thousands of Brits will spend their last pennies on going to New York to bear witness to this last rite for two of their heroes.

They are worth more, much more than Big Daddy Netflix and Uncle Saudi.

Meanwhile, the British Croquet Association beware.

Sports.title: Boxing champion Prichard Colon dies aged 33, 11 years after taking 'illegal' punches in fight which left him in a 221-day coma and a vegetative state
Sports.content:
Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33 more than a decade after suffering catastrophic brain injuries.

Back in October 2015 Colon, competing as a super-middleweight at the time, suffered a bleed on the brain after taking repeated blows to the back of the head during a contest with America's Terrel Williams in Virginia.

After vomiting and collapsing in the dressing room after his defeat, the Puerto Rican was rushed to hospital before spending 221 days in a coma. The fight with Williams had seen part of his skull collapse as a result of the repeated rabbit punches, which are deemed illegal in the sport.

After emerging from the coma, Colon, once a promising rising star in the ring, was left in a vegetative state with life-altering injuries. He was under the near-constant care of his family.

Colon conquered multiple national amateur championships and won a Youth Pan American gold medal before turning professional.

Colon's dad and former trainer, Richard, announced the heartbreaking news on social media, writing: 'Good morning, everyone. I regret to inform you of the passing of my son Prichard from this earthly world. He is now in a better place.'

He added: 'Thank you for so many years of love and prayers. As much as you can, please keep us in your prayers.'

Former boxer Prichard Colon has died at the age of 33, his family have announced

The Puerto Rican suffered catastrophic brain injuries during a 2015 fight (pictured)

Until that fateful fight almost 11 years ago, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects.

He had established an unblemished 16-0 record with 13 knockouts with many in boxing viewing him as a future star.

Following the bout against Williams, Colon was rushed to the hospital where doctors discovered a subdural hematoma.

He underwent emergency surgery as medics desperately attempted to relieve the swelling in his brain. After spending 221 days in a coma, Colon awoke unable to walk or talk.

Despite the traumatic injuries, just three years ago, Colon had vowed not to throw in the towel.

In an update on his Facebook profile at the time, Colon attempted to speak with his mother and even raised a smile in a moving video.

The post was captioned: 'I will not give up'.

In other clips, the ex-fighter could be seen attending a truck rally with his family, while also appearing to take a positive step in being able to brush his own teeth.

He was left in a vegetative state and was under the near-constant care of his family

Until that fateful fight, Colon had been one of the sport's most promising prospects

His mother also shared a video of her son on his 31st birthday where she gave him a cupcake with a candle on it.

Colon's story is one of the most tragic in boxing history, with former heavyweight champion Deontay Wilder breaking down in tears while discussing it last year.

'We’ve seen what happens, look at Colon. How he got hit, Prichard Colon, correct,' Wilder said.

'This man didn’t have no kids… they don’t understand. Y’all don’t f****** understand what we go through, man.

'And I don’t even know him like that, but I will always be an advocate for us. Because this man will never know what it’s like to be somebody’s father. And that’s one of the most precious things in the world, to be somebody’s father. But he will never be nobody’s father, man.

'Because he got in the ring to support his family but now, his family got to take care of him for the rest of his life.'

Sports.title: Red Bull officially named F1's best engine as FIA makes ADUO results public
Sports.content:
The FIA has published the results of the latest Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) evaluation for Formula 1 power units - with Red Bull-Ford still considered the benchmark.

According to the governing body’s analysis, which is inclusive of all races from the Melbourne season opener to round 11 at Budapest, the Red Bull-Ford internal combustion engine is the most powerful in F1.

Mercedes is 2-4% down on power, while Audi, Ferrari and Honda are more than 4% adrift; the Japanese manufacturer’s new powertrain, which was introduced at last weekend’s Dutch Grand Prix, was not taken into account.

After the first quarter of the 2026 season, Mercedes had been granted one additional homologation for 2026 and 2027 each, while Audi, Ferrari and Honda received two each for this year and next year too. This consists in additional cost cap allowance and further dyno tests.

However, no official announcement had been made. While the FIA did confirm the ADUO ranking today on Wednesday 26 August, no additional homologations have been awarded this time.

“The FIA has undertaken thorough and exhaustive analysis as part of our ADUO review process,” said the FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis.

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

“With the release of the findings of Period 2, we are confident that, based on the quality of the data, its analysis is incredibly robust, giving us a high level of confidence in our findings.

“We also have to respect the confidentiality and intellectual property of the teams and their power unit manufacturers in disseminating any details from the findings.

“This is the first year of ADUO so naturally there are areas which we may evolve over time, in discussion with all the PU manufacturers.”

ADUO has been at the receiving end of criticism with an obvious drawback being that it only considers the internal combustion engine, which is not the only performance differentiator in F1’s current hybrid power units.

Mercedes, not Red Bull-Ford, has widely been considered to have the most powerful engine, which even Silver Arrows boss Toto Wolff admitted - though he perhaps let his guard down when he made that comment, given he wasn’t referring to ADUO.

Red Bull in particular has been dismayed by the lack of opportunities afforded by the current ranking, requesting a review of the post-Canada results - which was unsuccessful.

“Toto is right. I also think that they have the most powerful power unit,” said Red Bull boss Laurent Mekies after the Belgian Grand Prix. “And certainly they had a sizeable advantage on the straight this weekend again.

“But it's not the first weekend. They have an advantage on the straight most weekends and this weekend a bit more with the track sensitivity. As you said, the second period closing in Budapest in a week's time. We'll see what's happening.”

Sports.title: McLaren denies Mercedes claim it cannot afford aggressive upgrades in F1 2026
Sports.content:
McLaren Formula 1 team principal Andrea Stella is sceptical about his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff's claims that Mercedes doesn't have the available budget to fast-track car upgrades.

In recent weeks Ferrari and especially McLaren have made drastic improvements to their 2026 cars, allowing them to take two wins apiece and put significant pressure on the erstwhile dominant Mercedes team.

Compared to its rivals, Mercedes has only trickled out a minimal quantity of aero upgrades, planning to bring a bigger package to October's Bahrain Grand Prix held in Malaysia.

That delay exposes Mercedes to further damage over the next three September rounds in Italy, Spain and Azerbaijan. But when asked by Autosport after the Dutch Grand Prix if those development decisions are now starting to become increasingly uncomfortable in light of McLaren's rapid progress, Wolff said his team's hands are tied with how Brackley has partitioned its $215m cost cap allowance.

"We haven't got the money to put developments on the car. I said before that we are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. But we just can't do what we can't do," the Austrian said.

"You will see towards the end of the season whether they are going to be able to deploy as much stuff onto the car as they do now. Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and the middle of the year than towards the end."

When those comments were put to McLaren chief Stella, he replied: "I would like to believe you, but I actually don't believe you."

Andrea Stella cast doubt on Mercedes' claims Photo by: Steven Tee / LAT Images via Getty Images

Stella was sceptical because the changes to the 2027 power unit regulations, which move F1 towards a 57-43 split between combustion power and electrical energy, but also affect certain areas of the car design, come with an additional $3m cost cap allowance to be used in 2026 or 2027 to help teams prepare for the changes.

If Mercedes really wanted to, Stella said, it could use that allowance to put upgraded car parts into production.

"All teams will have an allowance in their reporting for the cost cap," Stella said. "And if I'm not wrong, it's like three million that you can use in the 2026 reporting for cost cap calculations. And I'm sure that Mercedes, having seen that their rivals are kind of elevating the game, I'm sure they will now cash in on their development that surely is happening in the ground.

"I'm sure the car in the wind tunnel is quite a bit faster than the car they have on track and they will want to now convert some of this potential into upgrades that make it to the real car. So, I'm just pretty sure that they will have upgrades. Obviously, it would be good if not, but I don't even want to think about it..."

Sports.title: Hamilton claims Dutch GP radio outbursts weren't "the best version of me"
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says his Dutch Grand Prix frustration "wasn’t the best version of me" as he apologised to his Ferrari Formula 1 team for it boiling over on team radio.

During the second half of the race, Hamilton grew increasingly frustrated at the lack of strategy updates from Ferrari, especially once he got stuck behind team-mate Charles Leclerc, who was slower than the Briton on older tyres.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job,” a sarcastic Hamilton fired over on the airwaves once Leclerc finally pitted on lap 43.

After the race, Hamilton said Ferrari still had steps to make on race weekend execution, pointing to Mercedes' much slicker swap between George Russell and Kimi Antonelli as a source of inspiration.

But for Ferrari, the picture was a little bit more complicated than that, as the team was planning to pit Leclerc earlier but had to extend his stint for another lap to avoid traffic.

At the same time, the plan for Hamilton was to stay on track until the end of the race, but team principal Fred Vasseur explained Ferrari didn't want to alert its rivals to its strategy, so it decided not to communicate it straight away.

Charles Leclerc leading Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Taking to social media, Hamilton has now apologised to his team for his heated radio exchanges.

"I’ve listened back to some of my radio and TV comments. In the heat of the moment frustration can come out, especially when you care as deeply as I do," Hamilton wrote. "But that wasn’t the best version of me. I take responsibility for that, and I’ll be better.

"That passion comes from believing in this team, the people in it, and what we’re building together. The direction is clear. The belief is there. And the fight is absolutely still on."

Hamilton was buoyed by Ferrari's recent progress as its relentless car upgrade programme has allowed both him and Leclerc to win a grand prix, with Hamilton holding third in the drivers' championship on equal points with second-placed Russell.

"I’m incredibly proud of everyone back at the factory who continues to bring updates, find performance and push us forward," the seven-time world champion added.

"To the team at the track, thank you. The commitment and effort never go unnoticed. We still have work to do, particularly over one lap, but we’ll keep digging in, learning and improving together."

Eventually, a late virtual safety car helped Mercedes' Russell defend third place, with both Hamilton and Leclerc stranding off the podium in fourth and fifth.

Sports.title: McLaren appealing Monaco GP result "with a double intent"
Sports.content:
McLaren Formula 1 team principal Andrea Stella says its appeal against the Monaco Grand Prix result, which is being held on Tuesday, stems from its concern for "the integrity of the sport".

On Tuesday, the FIA's International Court of Appeal is handling an appeal by McLaren and Red Bull against the result of June's Monaco Grand Prix, in which several drivers were handed time penalties for exceeding pitlane speed limits, including McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Alpine driver Pierre Gasly.

Afterwards, it emerged those pitlane infractions were false flags, caused by a timing loop error at the start of Monaco's unique pit entry. All drivers, other than Gasly (and his Alpine team-mate Franco Colapinto), had already served their time penalties during the race, while the Frenchman was handed a double five-second time penalty at the flag, demoting him from third to seventh.

After Alpine launched a Right of Review against Gasly's penalties, the stewards rescinded both and restored the Frenchman's podium berth, which demoted Red Bull's Isack Hadjar to fourth and also bumped Piastri down the order.

As a result, both McLaren and Red Bull launched an appeal procedure, because they took issue with Gasly's penalty being rescinded while other drivers, including Piastri, had no such opportunity.

Anticipating the hearing, which takes place across Tuesday but could potentially drag on for longer, McLaren boss Stella said the team was both looking after its own interest in the constructors' standings and the interest of the series in general.

Monaco 2026 podium Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

"We go to the hearing at the International Court of Appeal with a double intent," Stella said on Sunday after the Dutch Grand Prix. "The first intent is more general than the interest of McLaren.

"We think that the process that happened after the race in Monaco needs to be reviewed because from fairness for all competitors, the fact that the penalty was removed introduces some significant elements of concern. And we would like to take the opportunity of the International Court of Appeal for a clarification of this aspect.

"There's obviously more related to this case. It can go into the technical aspects of how the pit limiter speed was calculated. But for me, at a high level, it's more the fairness and the principle that needs to be clarified and possibly reinstated."

He added: "The second aspect is the interest of McLaren ourselves. We were also materially penalised for having served a penalty that is not appealable and this cost us points in the championship.

"So, there's a general interest for Formula 1 and the integrity of the sport. And there's a material interest for McLaren in terms of our championship impact. These are the two points of view, the two perspectives that we would like to pursue and seek clarification for in the coming International Court of Appeal."

Sports.title: FIA condemns online abuse at F1 stewards following Colapinto's Dutch GP penalty
Sports.content:
Formula 1's governing body the FIA condemned the online harassment directed at its race stewards following their decision to apply the rulebook and penalise Alpine driver Franco Colapinto at Zandvoort.

Colapinto and Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad were both handed drive-through penalties for overtaking under a double-waved yellow flag on lap one of the race.

At the end of the lap, the yellows came out for a big crash involving Red Bull's Max Verstappen, which neutralised the final marshal sector until the start-finish straight.

The first half of lap two was green again until race control decided to throw a red flag. As the yellows came out, Colapinto completed an overtake on Racing Bulls driver Yuki Tsunoda coming out of Zandvoort's final corner, while Lindblad drafted past Alpine's Pierre Gasly before crossing the start-finish line, after both drivers had been forced to take evasive action for debris.

Referring to the Colapinto incident, the FIA stewards wrote: "Car 43 was behind Car 22 entering Turn 14 and overtook Car 22 in the double yellow flag sector before the line at the end of Lap 1.

"Normally, such infringement requires a 10-second stop-go penalty, but the Stewards acknowledge the complications caused by the significant amount of debris on track at this point and take this into account as mitigating circumstances."

The stewards also offered an identically phrased verdict for Lindblad.

Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Colapinto felt his penalty was "extremely harsh" as he overtook Tsunoda a split second after the yellows came out. However, according to the letter of the rulebook both drivers' penalties were clear-cut cases as the governing body takes safety related infractions particularly seriously.

Colapinto's Argentinian sponsor Mercado Libre went much further on social media, questioning the FIA stewards' integrity. "The Stewards are killing the integrity of F1. This season they are proving to be horrible and impacting race results," said Mercado Libre's chief marketing officer Sean Summers, who has since removed the post. "Incompetence? Dishonesty? Both? Something is seriously broken in that organisation's culture."

The sponsor's inflammatory comments further stoked the flames on social media as the FIA stewards received abusive threats, while Alpine's own social accounts were also targeted because a vocal subset of Argentinian fans felt the team did not back Colapinto enough in the case.

On Monday, Alpine stated: "We fully trust the FIA and the stewards when it comes to the policing of these rules and the application of sporting penalties during a live race scenario.

"We believe the penalties applied for yellow flag Infringements during the opening laps of the Dutch Grand Prix were indeed harsh, but acknowledge they fit the punishment based on the letter of the law and were consistently applied across all competitors and is something we can review and learn from as a team."

Franco Colapinto, Alpine Photo by: Andy Hone/ LAT Images via Getty Images

The FIA, which has established the United Against Online Abuse campaign to tackle online abuse in sport, is understood to be exploring legal options and has released the following statement.

"Following the Dutch Grand Prix, FIA stewards were targeted with online abuse after applying sporting penalties in line with FIA regulations," a statement read.

"The United Against Online Abuse Coalition condemns all forms of abuse and harassment. Disagreement with decisions is part of sport, but it must never justify threats or personal attacks.

"In 2023, the FIA launched the United Against Online Abuse Coalition after a steward faced targeted abuse following the United States Grand Prix. We urge everyone engaging with our sport to do so with respect and responsibility, online and offline."

Among the toxic abuse hurled at the FIA, it was suggested Colapinto was penalised because of his nationality, with there being perceived bias against non-British drivers.

Lindblad, who was given an identical penalty for a very similar infraction, is British.

Sports.title: Mercedes "hasn't got the money" to keep up with rival teams' F1 upgrades
Sports.content:
Mercedes Formula 1 team principal Toto Wolff says his squad "hasn't got the money" to develop its 2026 car as much as McLaren and Ferrari are doing.

Both McLaren and Ferrari have made significant progress in recent months by piling on upgrades to their respective cars, which has turned both into multiple race winners.

Meanwhile, a more conservative upgrade plan at Mercedes, with little significant updates since May's Canadian Grand Prix, has eroded the Brackley squad's initial dominance.

Speaking after McLaren's reigning world champion Lando Norris took his second consecutive grand prix win of 2026 in Zandvoort, Wolff said Mercedes isn't able to match what its rivals are doing in the 2026 development race.

When asked by Autosport if those development decisions are now starting to become increasingly uncomfortable in light of McLaren's rapid progress, Wolff said his team's hands are tied with how it has partitioned its $215m cost cap allowance.

"We haven't got the money to put developments on the car. I said before that we are trying to evenly split that through the season based on our calculations of when we can bring the biggest updates and optimising the championship points. But we just can't do what we can't do," the Austrian said.

"That's why it is a development race. If you bring an upgrade, each of the top teams will have a couple of tenths in it, at least, and that's what you lose. So, yeah, the ride has been a bit tougher than at the beginning of the year."

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bagnall / Sutton Images via Getty Images

When pressed on why Mercedes hasn't got the cost cap budget to bring upgrades when McLaren and Ferrari have, he replied: "You will see towards the end of the season whether they are going to be able to deploy as much stuff onto the car as they do now.

"Someone might have a different strategy in spending more at the beginning and the middle of the year than towards the end."

Mercedes isn't expected to bring any significant upgrades to the W17 until F1 heads overseas again, starting with the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.

Wolff pointed out that the picture would have looked differently if Mercedes hadn't struggled as much with the reliability of its power unit, which has cost both Kimi Antonelli and George Russell several dozens of points thus far and will lead to grid penalties down the line.

"Did we spend too much at the beginning and the initial development? I don't think so," he added. "I just think we are an organisation with a certain size and infrastructure.

"In that respect we had a really quick car. We left between 50 and 100 points on the table due to reliability issues. That would have given us a little bit more of a gap than we have today. And other than that, we are just continuing to execute what the plan was and what the financial realities mean for us."

Sports.title: What Ferrari actually meant to do when Hamilton felt like a "guinea pig" in Dutch GP
Sports.content:
Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has clarified what led to Lewis Hamilton’s radio outbursts during a tough Dutch Grand Prix weekend for the Formula 1 outfit.

The Scuderia finished off the podium for a second, consecutive race as Hamilton took fourth with team-mate Charles Leclerc in fifth – the reverse of Budapest – and it is clear what the defining moments were for Ferrari during Sunday’s 72-lap contest.

The first occurred midway through when Hamilton had just overtaken McLaren driver Oscar Piastri for fifth and started closing in on a much slower Leclerc. But due to the tight nature of Zandvoort, the seven-time world champion found it difficult to overtake and was therefore calling for team orders which didn’t arrive, allowing Lando Norris, plus Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, to increase their advantage up ahead.

“Great way of wasting time guys, good job!” snapped a sarcastic Hamilton, who eventually took fourth when Leclerc made his second pitstop on lap 43 – one tour after he was initially supposed to do so.

The assumption was that the Briton would come in for fresh tyres shortly afterwards, considering those around the Ferrari cars did the same, but the Scuderia opted to keep Hamilton out for much longer, which meant he eventually took the lead.

But Norris and Antonelli rapidly closed in on fresher tyres, and by lap 53 they were all within a second of each other. “Are you using me as a guinea pig?” quipped Hamilton, who was practically a sitting duck as the McLaren and Mercedes respectively overtook him on laps 54 and 55.

The Ferrari driver was essentially left in the dark as to why his second stint was so long - 30 laps - and it required a lap 55 virtual safety car caused by Esteban Ocon for the 41-year-old to ditch his hard tyres for a fresh set of softs.

Fred Vasseur Photo by: Eric Le Galliot

“We didn't want to tell him the strategy at this stage because we didn't want to disclose it to the competitors,” said Vasseur. “We wanted to keep him on track until the end, I think it would have been the right call.

“Charles was supposed to pit. We extended one lap and it was a kind of confusion. I'm not worried about this. Everybody will be back in the briefing. They will have a clear picture about the race.

“Charles was a bit frustrated at one stage about the compound. I think everybody was a bit lost about the compound. Norris started with mediums on the first start [before the red flag], then he moved to softs.

“The difference between the three compounds was very marginal today. It was difficult to have a clear picture on the strategy. Sometimes, we have to change the strategy or adapt, because we are trying to learn from the others. For them it's a bit frustrating.”

So it’s obvious what dominated discussions in Hamilton’s post-race media session, during which he called for Ferrari to have ‘better execution’. He cited his former team Mercedes as inspiration, considering the late team orders the Silver Arrows quickly deployed as Russell handed second to Antonelli on lap 65 after the championship leader took softs under the VSC, while the Briton stayed out on hards.

Russell initially told race engineer Marcus Dudley that “we’ve lost a double podium” as Hamilton closed in on his former team-mate, but the Mercedes driver held on for third and post-race said the swap was the correct decision.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Had it not been for the earlier fiasco with Leclerc, Hamilton reckons he’d have had a better shot at claiming a late podium and Vasseur echoed those comments, claiming “the execution today was not that good”.

“You can always say after the race that it would have been better to do it on lap 46,” the Frenchman added. “The story is that, when Lewis came back on Charles, we were expecting him to pit.

“Then we had someone in the shadow of the car. We asked him to do one lap more. You can't ask him to do one lap more and to swap positions in the straight line. It's not so easy. If I have a look at the race now, I can see the difference. The main issue is that we didn't tell Lewis that we were expecting him to go to the end. It was not a matter of pushing.”

The result leaves Ferrari 87 points behind leader Mercedes and 75 ahead of third-placed McLaren, which has taken consecutive wins from pole via Norris, with 11 rounds remaining.

Sports.title: Antonelli set for Italian GP grid penalty
Sports.content:
Mercedes has officially decided its Formula 1 world championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start from the back of the grid at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix after it decided to give him a new power unit, exceeding his allowance for the year.

Drivers are allowed to use up to four power units for the season, but Mercedes' reliability woes over the first half of the campaign meant it has always been a question of when, not if, its drivers were going to exceed that allowance and take a grid penalty.

Antonelli is currently already at the limit with his V6 and exhaust system, while Russell has no more room for either a combustion engine or turbocharger.

Antonelli had been in line for a grid drop at his home race in Monza in two weeks' time, and Mercedes has now officially confirmed it will change the title favourite's engine. The 19-year-old is set for a full power unit switch, which sets him up for a back-of-the-grid start.

"With Kimi we are taking the full thing," Wolff confirmed, dismissing the notion that Mercedes could have been tempted to take into account Monza being Antonelli's home race.

Photo by: Pauline Ballet - Formula 1

"In theory, our calculations say that that's the best track to take it. Obviously, our algorithms don't take nationality into consideration. But we are here to fight for a championship and not get the most PR. So, that's what we are going to do."

Russell is also set for grid drop down the line, though the Brackley team hasn't decided yet where the Briton will swap power units yet.

Russell only took his fourth power unit at the recent Hungarian Grand Prix, the final race before the summer break. That gives him more flexibility on mileage, though the team could still opt to add a fifth power unit to his pool of components at any time.

"With George, the discussions are ongoing about where to take it," Wolff said.

The next suitable opportunity after Monza could be Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which emphasises power unit performance and top speed while providing some overtaking opportunities to offset a grid drop.

Sports.title: Domenicali hopeful Verstappen’s new deal will end talk of F1 exit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Stefano Domenicali hopes Max Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract will put an end to claims he could leave Formula 1.

The Red Bull driver, who is one of the strongest critics of F1’s current regulations, said his uncertainty over agreeing a new deal with his team had been “mainly about actually continuing in Formula 1.”

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s Dutch Grand Prix, Domenicali said “the news of Max staying in Red Bull for the next couple of years is a cherry on the cake for this weekend.”

“It’s great news, [I’m] very proud and happy because Max is a world champion, world class person that has a great personality in the sport and I cannot see [imagine] Formula 1 without him.”

In May, Verstappen said it was “mentally not doable for me to stay” if F1 did not alter the power balance between the combustion and electrical parts of its engines next year. It subsequently announced changes will be introduced over the next two years.

“The rules are slowly getting a bit better and, let’s say, I’m willing to live with it,” said Verstappen. “Hopefully by 2030 it opens up another opportunity, potentially with V8 engines coming in, to look again.”

Domenicali hopes Verstappen’s new deal will quieten speculation the popular four-times champion will leave F1. “[I’m] very happy that this news now is official and all these talks that have been happening so far will be out of place,” he said. “Now I’m sure that the focus [will be] for the team to be as good as possible to give Max the best car that he can.”

Doubt continues to hang over the status of F1’s final two rounds this season, which will be held in the Middle East. The conflict in the region has already led F1 to abandon its plans to race in Saudi Arabia in Bahrain this year and arranged for the latter event to take place in Malaysia instead.

Domenicali indicated no decision has yet been taken to cancel the final two rounds in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. “The calendar, as I said, is confirmed, so there are still a few tickets to be sold in Abu Dhabi,” he said. “Everything is progressing well, and we stay focused on delivering the calendar we promised at the beginning of the year.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Lenient response to drivers passing red light sets bad precedent | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s stewarding guidelines state drivers should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties if they pass a red light at the pit lane exit during the grand prix.

However the stewards opted for much more lenient penalties when Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto broke the rule at Zandvoort last weekend. Reader @Alianora-La-Canta says this sets a bad precedent:

The drivers had no way to know that no dangerous situations would be created by ignoring the red light. Therefore a penalty should have been issued that involved a sporting disadvantage. Even mitigating the penalty would be risky, if understandable (due to the point of the procedure, I recognise the risk should have been much lower than usual). Now people are going to ignore the red light if they think it’s under a red flag and they think there’s an advantage in doing so, which is dangerous because the drivers do not have the information the FIA does.

Sports.title: Verstappen to race 100 drivers at once in karts at Silverstone | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen will take on 100 drivers in a special go-kart race at Silverstone, Red Bull has announced.

The four-times world champion will start at the back of the grid with 100 rivals ahead of him.

“In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking,” said Verstappen. “Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it’s always nice to return.

“It’s about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I’ve done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things. I will be looking forward to just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me.”

Red Bull say Verstappen’s rivals will be drawn “from every corner of sport and culture: from Red Bull athletes and celebrities to content creators, personalities and everyday fans invited from around the world.”

The event will take place on September 16th, three days after the Spanish Grand Prix, at a specially designed track at the home of the British Grand Prix.

“Creating a track for 100 drivers at the same time has never been done, never been seen,” said circuit designer and race director David Terrien. “So it’s very exciting.

“When you have Max Verstappen chasing everyone, I think that’s going to be the experience of a lifetime for all the drivers. You’re going to have Max showcasing all these skills of looking through the traffic, trying to prepare and plan where he can overtake people, and going through the traffic at the fastest speed he can because he doesn’t want to let the drivers at the front pull away.”

The event will be broadcast in some territories on Disney Plus and the ESPN app.

Sports.title: On This Day: Schumacher’s stunning debut ends early at Spa | Brief
Sports.content:
One of the most famous and consequential debuts in grand prix history came to a disappointingly early end 35 years ago today.

Michael Schumacher had already electrified the Formula 1 paddock at Spa-Francorchamps by putting Bertrand Gachot’s Jordan seventh on the grid. Unfortunately his clutch died as he pulled away from the grid, ending his race on the first lap.

The Jordans were quick at Spa – Schumacher’s team mate Andrea de Cesaris was closing on race leader Ayrton Senna until his Ford-Cosworth engine let him down. That left championship leader Senna to collect a valuable 10 points after title rival Nigel Mansell retired.

Sports.title: McLaren’s car is still “horrible to drive” despite consecutive wins, says Norris | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lando Norris may have won the last two grands prix in a row but he says McLaren’s car is still a handful to drive.

The world champion believes this is partly a consequence of the 2026 regulations.

“It’s tough to say, but I do think it’s a trickier car to drive this year in some ways,” said Norris. “I think you can see that because the gaps between team mates are often bigger this year, I would say, than it was last year.”

However Norris says he is doing better at communicating his needs to his team.

“I do believe I’m able to understand situations better, to understand the car in a better way,” he explained. “It’s still just horrible to drive, but I’m doing a better job at just understanding this, relaying this to my team, figuring stuff out.

“So, it’s not just that I’m driving better on track. I’m certainly eliminating my weaknesses on track, and I don’t have so many, but it’s also how I work off the track.”

He said the changes he made on his car between the sprint race and qualifying session in the Netherlands “is a perfect example of [how] the work we put in overnight transformed our race and gave me the opportunity to win.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris’s team mate Oscar Piastri also appeared to struggle with his car at times during Sunday’s race, where he finished sixth. At one stage he asked his race engineer Tom Stallard: “Please give me some help on how to drive this thing.”

Despite his wins in the last two rounds, Norris says McLaren must make significant improvements in their car’s low-speed cornering.

“We have a strong car in certain areas,” he said. “It’s not like last year where we were pretty good everywhere.

“We’re very, very strong in high speed, and that’s the place we’ve improved the car the most, is high-speed performance. No one matches us in high-speed, and that’s a good thing. My pace advantage to Mercedes in turn seven and eight was crazy, but the advantage that they have to us in slow speed is also crazy.

“Therefore, I don’t have the confidence to say, ‘Yeah, I can easily fight for a championship for the rest of the season.’ I know I’ve just won two races in a row and had two poles in a row, but at the minute I don’t have the car I need to fight for a championship.

“I know that’s quite a big comment, but I think last year I understood what is needed from a car and what was needed for myself. And I know the level that I am now and what I know I can perform at, and I know just what I need from the car and I know what tracks we have coming up where we’re going to certainly struggle more, and I don’t want to struggle more.

“So I’m just doing my part to make sure, as a team, we don’t relax, we don’t get complacent in any way, and we work more than we’ve ever done before, even more than the last two years when we’ve won championships. I need the guys and girls to work and focus better than ever before to improve on these areas. If we can improve on these slow speeds, I’m confident that I can win every race this season. If we don’t, then it’s much more difficult to believe so.”

Charles Leclerc was in no doubt Ferrari wanted him to pit when he was holding his team mate up during the Dutch Grand Prix.

Hamilton was becoming increasingly infuriated, telling the team “we’re just losing time.” After Leclerc finally pitted on the next lap, following another instruction from Ferrari, Hamilton sarcastically commented: “Big waste of time guys, good job.”

The Ferrari drivers finished the race behind Russell, with Hamilton fourth ahead of Leclerc.

Sports.title: Shannon Briggs Claims Tommy Fury Fight Talks
Sports.content:
“I just got off the phone negotiating a fight with Tommy Fury. All I can say is Tommy, don’t get scared now. Don’t get scared, Tommy. Tell your daddy and your big brother I’m coming for you. You first, daddy second, other one third. Let’s go, Tommy. Let’s go, champ,” said Briggs via talkSPORT Boxing.

His last fight came on May 21, 2016, when he stopped Emilio Ezequiel Zarate in the first round at London’s O2 Arena. BoxRec lists Briggs as inactive, with 60 wins, six losses, one draw, one no contest and 53 knockouts.

Ten years away is the real story behind the proposed fight. Briggs possesses an enormous size advantage and remains recognizable, but he would be returning at 54 against an active 27-year-old cruiserweight. Tommy Fury had just celebrated his 17th birthday when Briggs made his last professional appearance.

Following the Tyson-Paul Formula

The commercial idea is easy to understand. Jake Paul’s fight with a 58-year-old Mike Tyson demonstrated how much attention can be created by matching a young crossover boxer with a heavyweight star from a previous generation. Briggs may see an opportunity to collect his own payday while that market still exists.

His punching power gives promoters something to sell, but his present reflexes, punch resistance and stamina are unknown. Victories over George Foreman and Siarhei Liakhovich belong to another era. The last time Briggs faced world-class opposition was his punishing 12-round loss to Vitali Klitschko in 2010.

Licensing requires more than an agreement between the fighters. The British Boxing Board of Control requires medical and optician reports, brain scans and blood testing before granting a boxer’s license. It has the authority to reject a contest it considers an extreme mismatch. Age alone does not make sanctioning impossible, as Tyson’s professional fight with Paul showed, but Briggs’ inactivity requires serious scrutiny.

This proposal reveals where Tommy Fury’s career is heading. He has the age, family connections and background to pursue active cruiserweights, yet his largest financial opportunities continue to come from crossover events. After facing Jake Paul, KSI and Eddie Hall, fighting Briggs would take him even farther from domestic titles and rankings.

Misfits may see value in Briggs’ personality, American following and “Let’s go, champ” catchphrase. That does not make the contest competitive. It makes Briggs another famous older heavyweight whose past can be sold to an audience that remembers him more clearly than the fighter he is at 54.

Briggs remains the only party claiming negotiations have occurred. Until Fury or Misfits confirms the discussion, this is an attempted comeback pitch rather than evidence that a deal is close.

Sports.title: Nikita Tszyu Admits Mahoney Edged Split Draw
Sports.content:
Mahoney began quickly behind his jab and higher output, taking advantage of Tszyu’s measured start. A clash of heads opened a cut above Tszyu’s right eye in the third round, yet the southpaw settled into the fight and began landing his heavier left hands and body shots. Tszyu controlled portions of the middle rounds with pressure and power. Mahoney never allowed him to take complete command, countering and forcing exchanges at close range.

The hometown fighter finished strongly during the final four rounds. His activity and right hands gave him an argument for the decision, while Tszyu still landed the more damaging individual punches.

Tszyu Questions the Official Result

Rather than defend the 117-111 card in his favor, Tszyu conceded that Mahoney had done enough to win.

“I gave the fight to Ben honestly; he was one hell of a tough fight,” Tszyu said after the decision, as quoted by Nine. “It was a close fight, but I thought he edged it.”

That admission says more about the contest than the wide Tszyu scorecard. He was the favorite, the bigger puncher and the fighter being positioned for an eventual opportunity against IBF champion Josh Kelly. Mahoney was supposed to test him, not leave Tszyu questioning if he had been beaten.

The draw does not ruin Tszyu’s championship ambitions, but it changes how his readiness should be judged. Mahoney’s jab, durability and late output exposed areas that had not been tested during Tszyu’s rise.

A rematch would provide a clean answer. Moving Tszyu directly toward Josh Kelly after a performance he believed he lost would leave a more uncomfortable question behind.

Sports.title: Aloys Junior Loses Mike Perez Fight Saturday
Sports.content:
The original matchmaking was risky from the beginning. The Cuban southpaw is 40, and Queensberry was relying on an aging fighter to complete camp and reach fight night. His withdrawal has left Junior with a substitute who will have only a few days to prepare.

Perez still would have given Junior a specific technical test. His southpaw stance, experience and counterpunching would have forced the 23-year-old to manage distance, adjust to different angles and avoid becoming reckless when attacking.

Musah presents a completely different style after Junior spent camp preparing for Perez. That may require a quick tactical adjustment, but it turns the bout into an exercise in patience rather than the carefully chosen test Queensberry originally planned.

At 35, Musah has a modest 4-2-1 record, although he is not as weak as those numbers suggest. He stopped 14-2 Nathan Quarless in March after dropping him in the fifth and sixth rounds. Neither of his two defeats came inside the distance, and he has completed two ten-round fights.

Reducing the contest from ten rounds to six limits what Junior can learn from it. He must build stamina, manage his pace and think clearly when tired. Even if Musah lasts, six rounds will not replicate the physical and mental strain found against leading cruiserweights. The replacement also puts Junior in a no-win situation. An early knockout will be dismissed as the predictable result against a fight-week substitute. If Musah takes him six rounds or makes him look sluggish, questions will be asked about his readiness for better opposition.

The promotional purpose is obvious. Junior has not fought since defeating Ellis Zorro by unanimous decision in July 2025. Keeping him active, placing him before a large crowd and giving viewers another look at his power all benefit Queensberry.

Activity and development are not the same. Viddal Riley, Cheavon Clarke and Isaac Chamberlain have already competed in meaningful domestic fights. Junior requires that level of opposition if Queensberry wants to move him toward British, European and world honors.

Appearing against Musah may fill a space on the prelims, but sitting out and returning in a properly prepared ten-round contest would do more for Junior’s career.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sees Frank Sanchez Testing Itauma
Sports.content:
That performance showed why Sanchez is dangerous for Itauma. He is not another aging heavyweight brought in to stand directly in front of the 21-year-old and disappear after absorbing the first clean combination. His movement, counterpunching and durability may keep him in the fight long enough to test Itauma’s chin more than once.

“He’s very clever, and he’s old,” Tony Bellew said.

Officially, Sanchez is 34, the same age as Hrgovic, making the repeated references to him being old strange unless Hearn and Bellew doubt his listed age.

Hearn considers Hrgovic’s upright style a better tactical fit for Itauma. The Croatian is easier to locate and more likely to exchange at close range. Sanchez creates different questions by changing distance, moving laterally and waiting for an opponent to overcommit.

Queensberry has spent years presenting Itauma as 24-karat gold while matching him with aging heavyweights whose styles advertise his best qualities. They have generally lacked the foot speed and defensive movement to escape his combinations. Hrgovic is considerably better than those opponents, but his upright stance and willingness to exchange still give Itauma a stationary target.

A Sanchez upset would begin with surviving the first four rounds, moving laterally and forcing Itauma to reset before launching his left hand. Rather than trying to overpower him, the Cuban can draw out the initial attack, step away and counter while Itauma is recovering his position. Every missed rush would make the younger fighter expend energy without getting the spectacular finish his promoters and the crowd anticipate.

Itauma has never been forced to think under pressure against a puncher with Sanchez’s power, defend against counters or manage his pace deep into a championship fight. If he becomes impatient, Sanchez has the timing and single-shot power to make him pay. Itauma may have the answers, but nothing he has done in the ring has shown them yet.

Under the IBF arrangement, Queensberry has little room to continue the same matchmaking formula. The winner must face Sanchez within six months without an intervening bout unless the organization grants an exception. If Itauma wins Saturday, his team must either accept the most complicated stylistic opponent of his career, seek another delay or surrender the belt.

The repeated effort to label Sanchez “old” is worth challenging. He and Hrgovic are both officially 34, yet Hrgovic is promoted as Itauma’s first legitimate test while Sanchez is discussed as a fading veteran. The difference is not age. Sanchez simply presents a more difficult style for the type of opponents Queensberry has matched Itauma against.

Sports.title: Oba Carr Had the Tools to Beat Spence
Sports.content:
Speed was not Carr’s only weapon in this hypothetical matchup. In the second round of his December 1994 title fight with Trinidad, he timed a quick right hand that dropped the dangerous champion. Trinidad recovered and stopped Carr in the eighth, but the knockdown showed Carr’s ability to identify an opening and punish an elite puncher ahead of the return fire.

That straight right would be especially important against the southpaw Spence. Carr had the hand speed to fire between Spence’s deliberate advances, then follow with combinations that prevented Spence from establishing his body attack. Crawford used different footwork and possessed a far broader offensive arsenal, but Carr owned enough of the necessary tools to exploit the same declining reactions.

Further evidence came during Carr’s 12 rounds with Quartey, whose stiff jab was faster and more punishing than Spence’s. Two judges had Quartey well ahead, so the majority decision was not as close as the official result suggests. Carr still handled that jab for the full distance and continued returning fire against a powerful natural welterweight.

The 2019 car crash, retinal injury and years of forcing his body down to 147 gradually removed Spence’s best qualities. He defeated Yordenis Ugas, but no longer possessed the reactions or physical condition of his earlier years. By the Crawford fight, he looked depleted and was taken apart in nine rounds.

Prime Spence would make it a much closer contest. His size, body punching and physical pressure would test Carr, who was dropped twice by former lightweight champion Livingstone Bramble before escaping with a disputed split decision in 1991. The damaged Spence seen later in his career would struggle to impose those advantages early enough to stop Carr’s speed from taking control.

The depth of the 1990s placed Trinidad, Quartey, De La Hoya and Pernell Whitaker at the top of the division. Missing out on a belt against those champions did not place Carr below championship level. In Spence’s fragmented era, he would have found several opportunities to collect one.

An empty championship column hides Carr’s quality. He had the speed, power and experience to beat the diminished Spence, even if Crawford remained a level beyond him.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Begins His Path To Undisputed Welterweight Champion
Sports.content:
Lopez told the media at the post-fight press conference of the younger version of himself who would get mad at not being able to land against his opponent and would invite his opponent to hit him; that’s the fighter in him that welcomes a war.

https://x.com/ShakurStevenson/status/2091592063011946634?s=20

Teo outlanded Rolly 124 to 73 in total punches, outlanding him in 10 of 12 rounds. He was almost more effective offensively, having a better connection rate in both jabs (17.7%) and power punches (34.6). Romero was extremely economical with his punches, with a very low output, landing a single-digit number of punches in 11 of 12 rounds (Compubox). Former opponent Shakur Stevenson spoke of Lopez’s ability on X and what makes him special: “Teo has some sort of ability to make other fighters not throw a lot of punches and move a lot more than their usual style. I seen it with Loma, Ortiz, Sandor Martin, and now Rolly. Nonetheless, Teo did what he could with the style that was presented and got the job done!”

Teo stated at the post-fight presser he felt Rolly was not active enough and did not do enough to win the fight and thus is not deserving of a rematch. Romero expressed after that fight that he felt he won and did enough to merit a rematch. However, with no rematch clause in the contract, it is unlikely one will be given.

Teo stated at the post-fight presser his ultimate goal is to become undisputed champion, saying the following, “I got four fights, well now three fights with DAZN and all are road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no defense, no nothing, so whoever is next we’re going for them.” The other current champions in the division are (WBC) Ryan Garcia, (IBF) Liam Paro, and (WBO) Devin Haney. Only Ryan has a fight scheduled, and Garcia did express interest in fighting the winner of Romero-Lopez; however, he must first get by Conor Benn. After the fight, Paro congratulated Teo on X, saying, “Teofimo Lopez congrats, let’s unify.”

As to who he fights next remains to be seen, but Lopez did express to the media that the current champions he would like to face are Haney last and earn his undisputed designation against him due to the controversy that occurred at lightweight when Teo was not recognized as the undisputed champion at lightweight. Lopez has demonstrated throughout his career that he does not fear fighting the best and continues his search for greatness as he continues his path to becoming undisputed welterweight champion.

Sports.title: Boxing’s Biggest Stars Were Never Universally Loved
Sports.content:
Joe Louis reached an even broader audience. His 25 consecutive heavyweight title defenses remain a division record, but his importance extended beyond the ring. Louis conducted exhibitions during World War II and served in the Army, becoming a national figure at a time when Black athletes faced severe racial barriers.

Sugar Ray Robinson followed as one of boxing’s most admired performers. His speed, combination punching and long career helped establish the standard by which later pound-for-pound greats were judged. Henry Armstrong defeated 16 world champions and once held the featherweight, lightweight and welterweight titles at the same time. His nonstop attacking style made him a fan favorite.

Rocky Marciano finished his career at 49-0 with 43 stoppages. His knockout victory over an aging Joe Louis was one of the best-known wins on his record.. Manny Pacquiao later became an international attraction, winning titles across eight divisions and carrying the expectations of the Philippines whenever he fought.

Not every major attraction was universally liked. Jack Johnson became heavyweight champion during an era of open racial hostility. Much of the opposition to him came from white Americans who resented seeing a Black champion defeat white challengers. The search for a “Great White Hope” revealed more about the country than it did about Johnson’s popularity. He was a hero to many Black fans while being vilified elsewhere.

Pernell Whitaker never generated the same commercial following as several less-accomplished fighters. His defensive style required viewers to appreciate positioning, timing, and subtle movement rather than constant exchanges. When I once asked him to name his toughest opponent, he replied, “All of them!”

Larry Holmes also struggled to receive the appreciation his ability deserved. He followed Muhammad Ali, defeated an aging version of him, and later angered Marciano supporters by saying, “Rocky couldn’t carry my jockstrap” after losing to Michael Spinks. That bitterness overshadowed a heavyweight reign that included 20 successful title defenses.

Ali demonstrated how hostility itself could be turned into business. His boasting encouraged some spectators to adore him and others to pay in hopes of watching him lose. I met him at his Cherry Hill, New Jersey, home in 1973 and again at his Deer Lake, Pennsylvania, training camp in 1977. Away from the cameras, he was far different from the confrontational character used to sell fights.

Ricky Hatton, Mike Tyson, Marvin Hagler, Sugar Ray Leonard, Willie Pep and Alexis Arguello also built devoted followings through different combinations of personality, nationality and fighting style. I met all except Hatton and found each of them to be a gentleman.

The history shows why ranking boxers only as “popular” or “unpopular” is too simple. Some were loved, some were resented, and a select few became enormous attractions by giving audiences reasons to feel both.

Sports.title: Ade Oladipo Misreads George Foreman’s Place in History
Sports.content:
“That’s horrendous,” Ade said. “What? Because he can sell grills, all of a sudden he can fight?”

He then assigned almost all the Rumble in the Jungle’s importance to Muhammad Ali, arguing that Ali could have faced someone else and produced the same event.

“I’d never heard anything about Foreman,” Oladipo said. “That is all Muhammad Ali.”

During his interview with Helwani, Oladipo first claimed the clip had been taken out of context. He described the original exchange as a light argument over the most famous boxer ever, with Gough bringing up the Foreman grill while Oladipo defended Ali. That account softened the substance of his own remarks.

“It wasn’t necessarily anti-George Foreman. I think it was so pro-Ali that I was like, ‘No, no, my guy,’” Oladipo told Ariel Helwani. “I was just saying my guy is numero uno, and by defending my guy kind of shot down others… I certainly didn’t mean to be disrespectful to the late, great George Foreman… I was just trying to back my guy, and I think maybe I batted a bit too hard.”

That is closer to an admission than a defense. Oladipo knew while recording the segment that his remarks might generate criticism. He now accepts that Foreman was one of the greatest heavyweights ever and that he unfairly diminished him while arguing for Ali.

Before making that concession, Oladipo spent several minutes attacking his critics. He called them jealous, dismissed some as “minions” and suggested members of the boxing media were using the clip to pursue his broadcasting position. He also complained that boxing expects commentators to possess the equivalent of a university doctorate in the sport’s history.

Born in 1981, Oladipo was not around for Foreman’s rise. He never experienced the sequence of an Olympic gold medalist developing into boxing’s most destructive heavyweight, wiping out established champions and arriving in Zaire with the aura of an unbeatable force.

Foreman’s 1973 destruction of Joe Frazier remains among boxing’s most memorable title changes. Howard Cosell’s repeated cry of “Down goes Frazier” entered American sports culture as Foreman dropped the champion six times in two rounds.

Frazier had defeated Ali two years earlier. Ken Norton had broken Ali’s jaw and beaten him in 1973. Foreman needed only two rounds to destroy Norton, then later stopped Frazier for a second time.

He was the Mike Tyson of an earlier generation. Spectators watched because Foreman’s knockouts carried a frightening inevitability. Ali supplied unmatched personality and global celebrity in Zaire, while the champion across from him represented terrifying physical danger.

Claiming that Ali could have fought anyone in Kinshasa and created the same spectacle also reduces Ali’s accomplishment. The Rumble in the Jungle achieved immortality because Ali conquered the undefeated destroyer whom many believed might seriously hurt him. Replace Foreman with a routine contender and the event becomes another Ali title fight rather than a defining moment in sports history. Foreman’s reputation was not incidental to the legend. It was the obstacle that made Ali’s victory extraordinary.

The grill argument reverses the cause and effect. Foreman’s fame did not originate with kitchen appliances. Their enormous commercial success relied on a recognizable former heavyweight champion with an extraordinary personal story. Modern casual fans may associate the older, smiling Foreman with television commercials, but audiences in the 1970s knew him as an intimidating knockout artist.

His second career further weakens Oladipo’s dismissal. Foreman returned after a decade away, rebuilt himself in public and knocked out Michael Moorer in 1994 to regain the heavyweight championship at age 45. That accomplishment introduced him to another generation and completed a remarkable reinvention. His popularity rested on the combination of his terrifying first reign, historic comeback, and transformed personality. The grill capitalized on that story; it did not create it.

A broadcaster does not need personal memories of every boxing era. Curiosity is supposed to fill that absence. Foreman’s rise is not obscure material from 1922, as Oladipo’s comparison suggested. The heavyweight era containing Ali, Foreman, Frazier and Norton is foundational knowledge for anyone paid to discuss boxing professionally.

Calling critics jealous avoids that distinction. They were not demanding expertise in forgotten bare-knuckle champions. The criticism followed because a prominent broadcaster showed limited preparation on one of the sport’s central figures, then treated the reaction as an attempt to take his job.

The mistake was not choosing Ali as the more famous man. It was mistaking the older George Foreman Oladipo knew for the young fighter the world feared. Blaming the reaction on missing context and professional jealousy does not correct that historical blind spot.

Ghana News.title: Naming persons of interest in AKSA case is a step towards accountability – Mary Addah
Ghana News.content:
Transparency International Ghana Executive Director Mary Addah says the Office of the Special Prosecutor’s (OSP) decision to name persons of interest in the Ghanaian dimension of the Asante Kweku Berko bribery case is a positive step towards accountability.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 26, Madam Addah stressed that being named a person of interest does not imply guilt and should not be interpreted as a finding of wrongdoing.

She said publicly identifying the individuals who were in positions of authority during the period under investigation helps provide clarity on who was responsible for supervising the issues surrounding the AKSA deal.

"As indicated, being a person of interest doesn't make you guilty. So naming you as a person of interest doesn't count or take away from you.

“So it's a good step in the accountability drive because we've been asking ourselves, so who are these persons who are supposed to have presided over the issues and the concentration when it comes to the AKSA? Now, without a doubt, we know these were the people who were superintending,” she said.

Her comments follow the OSP’s identification of former Power Minister Kwabena Donkor and four others as its main persons of interest in its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the case.

The other persons named are Francis Walkson Kwesi Gyata, a former technical adviser to the Minister of Power; Solomon Adjetey Sowah, a former deputy director at the Ministry of Power; Lindin George Nii Mettle, a former director at Tricop Group Limited; and Baffour Ankomah Brobbey, an employee of Tricop Group Limited.

The development follows the conviction of Asante Kweku Berko by a federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, on August 3, 2026, over a bribery scheme involving more than US$1 million.

Berko, a dual citizen of Ghana and the United States and former Managing Director of the Tema Oil Refinery, was convicted over allegations that he conspired to pay bribes to multiple Ghanaian officials between 2014 and 2015.

The alleged payments were linked to the development and financing of a 370-megawatt fuel oil plant in Tema under an agreement involving the Government of Ghana, Turkish energy company AXA Energy Eratim and Goldman Sachs.

Mr Agyebeng said the OSP had provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation through Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework.

He added that the US Department of Justice had acknowledged the OSP’s assistance in the successful prosecution.

Ms Addah said whether the persons named by the OSP bear responsibility beyond their roles as persons of interest must be determined through the investigative process.

“As to whether it elevates them beyond that, it's an issue that the investigative bodies bring attention to,” she said.

Ghana News.title: Recycle Up! Ghana calls for more government support to expand green entrepreneurship
Ghana News.content:
Director of Operations at Recycle Up! Ghana, Gertrude Mawuena Goh, has called for increased government and corporate funding to expand opportunities for young entrepreneurs in the country’s circular economy, as the organisation continues efforts to build businesses from the country’s waste challenges.

According to her, inadequate funding remains a major hindrance to creating opportunities for the youth in the green economy.

She made the call at the RUG Incubation Programme Cohort 6 Demo Day held at the KIC Centre of Excellence in Ejisu, under the theme, “Empowering Innovation for Sustainable Business Growth.”

“We want the government to provide us with the network and also the funding support to enable us to us build more capacities of the youths in the secular economy space, so far, we had just a few engagements with the government like the NEIP Adwumawura program which we were privileged to train some startups in the Ashanti region.

Through that we were able to raise some funding to support the work we do, so more of such initiatives that can directly support us will be beneficial,”she asserted.

The RUG Incubation Programme, which has been running since 2019, targets young people between 18 and 35 years, particularly early-stage social entrepreneurs developing solutions in waste management, the circular economy and green business.

Participants receive training in financial management, fundraising, investor pitching, product and idea validation, business development, legal issues and market development.

Previous cohorts have also benefited from prototype funding and opportunities to pitch their businesses to investors.

Ms Goh said RUG’s work seeks not only to improve livelihoods but also to address the growing waste challenge, particularly waste that chokes drains and contributes to environmental degradation.

She, however, said inadequate funding remains a major challenge to expanding the organisation’s impact and called for stronger government and corporate support.

Ms Goh said RUG has so far impacted more than 35,000 people through its various interventions, stressing that the organisation’s work goes beyond incubation to include environmental awareness and behaviour-change programmes.

She said RUG also intends to expand its incubation programme to more young people across the country while strengthening its nationwide waste education campaign.

“Through the nationwide waste education campaign, we visit basic schools and sometimes senior high schools and we found environmental school clubs basically teaching them about waste management which focus on plastic waste, how they can reduce waste and also empower the schools to segregate plastic waste so that it feeds into the recycling value chain and we have launched a waste management hand book that we use in these environmental awareness education campaigns,” she added.

The Cohort 6 Demo Day featured seven start-ups and 13 entrepreneurs who pitched their businesses and products to investors and industry stakeholders.

The start-ups are focused on converting waste and agricultural by-products into products ranging from furniture and cosmetics to animal feed, reusable sanitary products, fabrics, packaging and fruit-based beverages.

Ecofurn, which repurposes rice husks, groundnut husks and plastic waste into durable, insect-resistant, water-resistant and eco-friendly school desks, emerged as the overall winner and received GH¢7,000.

Ellora Cosmetics, which produces rice shampoo bars, conditioners and face and body scrubs from waste rice, placed second with GH¢5,000, while Jostimo, a producer of pelletised animal feed from agricultural waste and by-products, placed third and received GH¢3,000.

For Ellora Cosmetics co-founder Theodora Dankwah and her partner, Louisa Yeboah, the programme provided an important opportunity to move their start-up beyond simply producing products to understanding their customers and building a sustainable business.

Ms Dankwah said her personal struggle with acne and unsuccessful attempts with different skincare products inspired the development of Ellora Cosmetics.

She said the company uses rice in its products, drawing inspiration from the popularity of rice-based skincare products, particularly in Korea.

“As a startup, we’ve always been searching for opportunities and how to bring our business into the spotlight so we saw the RUG Incubation Program opportunity on LinkedIn and we took the chance to apply.

It has been an eye-opening journey for us because at first we were going to stores to give them our products but coming to RUG Incubation Program, we knew that it does not just start from you doing the product but it starts from you knowing your customers and what they’re going through to come up with your products, "she said.

Ms Dankwah identified regulatory requirements, particularly certification by the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA), as one of the major challenges confronting the start-up.

She appealed to government and relevant stakeholders to introduce a simplified support package for start-ups in the food and cosmetics sectors to make regulatory certification more accessible.

“We’re calling on the government to bring in a small package for we the startups because even now if you want to open a bank account, some of the banks require FDA certificate before especially if you are in the food and cosmetics industry before they can open an account for you.

And looking at the processes, that FDA has to go through and the business registration has to go through, it makes it very difficult for we that startups to acquire that certificate. We call on the government to give us a package that will fasten the process for us, "she appealed.

The other participating start-ups were NafiPad, which produces reusable period pads from natural, breathable and biodegradable fabrics; FIBRELUX, which produces sustainable fabrics from plantain stems; Yarps Food, which processes cassava into shelf-stable flour and converts cassava peels and other waste into biodegradable packaging; and Vitazobo, which processes fruits into tea bags to extend their shelf life and reduce spoilage.

The seven start-ups and their entrepreneurs are part of RUG’s broader effort to promote youth-led innovation, waste reduction and sustainable enterprise development in Ghana’s circular economy.

The Demo Day winners were Ecofurn, which placed first and took home GH¢7,000, Ellora Cosmetics, which placed second with GH¢5,000, and Jostimo, which placed third, winning GH¢3,000.
