World.title: Time to 'recalibrate': Olympic figure skating champion Liu to miss season
World.content:
Olympic gold medallist figure skater Alysa Liu has said she will sit ​out the upcoming season to fine-tune her technique but reassured fans she would return to the sport.

Liu became ​the first ‌American woman since 2002 to capture Olympic gold in women's singles at this year's Milano ‌Cortina Games, where she also helped ⁠the United States to gold in ‌the team event.

"I ​always want to ‌challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry and skating can evolve," Liu wrote in a social media post, ​adding ‌that she would take time to "recalibrate".

Loading Instagram content

"It's important to me that my sport ⁠reflects my personal ‌growth.

"So fear not, I'll ‌be back, and in the meantime I'll be ‌rooting for my teammates near and far."

In an interview with ‌NBC ​Sports on Tuesday, ⁠Liu said she was planning to work on her "overall artistry, spins, jumps, everything" during her break from competition and ⁠intended to return in the 2027-28 season.

Winter Olympics live blog Alysa Liu becomes the first American woman to win singles figure skating gold in 24 years, completing her comeback after retiring in 2022 when she was only 16 years old.

"I just felt this ‌was ‌right. So I'm trusting my ​instincts," she said.

The announcement marks the latest change in a roller-coaster career for Liu, who arrived at the 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics and finished sixth.

She won bronze at the world titles a few months later before "retiring" from the sport at the age of 16, saying that skating "takes up your whole life, almost".

When she returned to skating she had a new look, with bleached stripes in her hair and a frenulum piercing — and a new approach and confidence that saw her win the world title in 2025 before gold at Milano Cortina.

Liu said her new approach to her sport and to life was more important than results.

Now she leaves to dream it all up again.

Reuters / ABC

World.title: Hird has chance to finally deliver true unity Essendon seeks
World.content:
When new Essendon coach Mark McVeigh was flanked by president Andrew Welsh and CEO Tim Roberts at his introductory press conference on Wednesday, there was a clear theme emanating from the day: unity.

Unity is the thing Essendon has strived for, and failed to find, for the last two decades as it has cycled through players, coaches and administrators in a bid to end an infamous finals drought.

Welsh hopes that by hiring McVeigh he is able to kill two birds with one stone.

McVeigh to canvass Hird return as icon urges Bombers fans to unite Mark McVeigh and Andrew Welsh are set to approach James Hird about a role at the club after he was overlooked to return as the senior coach for a second time.

The process to find its next coach acted as a litmus test for Essendon to actually show it had changed as a club after years of saying it with no actions to follow.

When Brad Scott was ousted midway through the season and James Hird launched his candidacy on national TV in the same week, the consensus was that Hird's return to the Bombers coaches box was a fait accompli.

The lack of belief or trust in Essendon as a sporting organisation left candidates pulling out, believing the club's trumpeted 'process' was actually a sham designed to deliver Hird the role.

It proved to be anything but, as Hird himself revealed after being beaten by McVeigh, leaving both he and Essendon at a potentially pivotal crossroads.

This rejected bid to be Essendon's coach is completely different to Hird's last rejection, when he finished second behind Brad Scott.

James Hird (centre) was left on the outside looking in when Brad Scott (left) won Essendon's coaching race in 2022. (Getty Images: James Wiltshire)

There was something symbolic in Hird, one of Essendon's favourite sons, being beaten out by Scott, a nemesis of his from the Brisbane Lions heyday.

Scott winning the coaching race was reminiscent another occasion where he'd famously got one over Hird, overpowering the under-cooked then-Essendon skipper on the wing during a key period in the 2001 grand final.

Scott, having arrived from the AFL and being selected by an independent panel, appeared a choice that was an aggressive attempt to get away from the fabric of Essendon.

Scott's regime brought a lot of change, and while his decisions may eventually age well, they left Essendon's diehards feeling more disillusioned with every loss that followed.

Andrew Welsh (left) and Mark McVeigh (right) are keen for Hird to return to the club in an official capacity. (Getty Images: Quinn Rooney)

Hird wasn't exactly forbidden from returning to Essendon while Scott was in charge, but he also wasn't welcomed with open arms.

This time around is different as both McVeigh and Welsh prepare to launch full-court presses to get Hird back through the doors, just not as the coach.

While the knock on Hird's coaching bid was his lack of experience in a recent AFL coaches box, what cannot be disputed is his knowledge of the game.

If Hird is able to get past the itch of being the coach, he could prove to be an incredible asset as either a football boss, or as a developmental coach. The opportunities are endless, given Essendon has basically wiped out its entire football department.

James Hird (left), Dean Solomon (centre) and Mark McVeigh (right) have the opportunity to link up under one roof again. (Getty Images: Daniel Pockett)

Having held the belief that McVeigh would have come with him had he been successful, as he also pledged to do in 2022, Hird now has the chance to repay the favour.

Welsh has hinted at Essendon bolstering its football department with key appointments in the coming months as it looks to surround McVeigh with a strong staff. It could do worse than bringing Hird back into the fold.

It is notable that Hird, while not receiving the job he wanted, mentioned he has experienced healing during the process in the form of mending fences with individuals he had fallen out with over the club's supplements scandal.

Hird is smart enough to know what his decision from this point on has the potential to do to his beloved club.

As Essendon desperately seeks unity, Hird's return would guarantee it, and he knows that. It is hard to see him turning his back on Essendon to try and coach elsewhere, even if that means he never gets to coach again.

At the front of Hird's mind will be two scenarios: winning Essendon's next premiership, but not as the coach, or winning a premiership elsewhere as the coach. He must figure out which of those will make him happiest.

The benefits of the McVeigh hire are two-fold for Essendon.

He has spent significant time in the coaches' boxes of two teams that have enjoyed deep September runs, albeit without winning the whole lot.

Loading Instagram content

McVeigh's history of working with both the Allies and the Swans Academy was a major selling point given Essendon's list demographic.

Critics suggesting McVeigh's hire was simply a case of jobs for mates were disrespectful to both his decade of coaching reps as well as Welsh's ability to be a professional.

Contrary to all the hysteria about Essendon only hiring "Essendon people", McVeigh is the first Essendon person to be hired as the club's senior coach since Hird's departure in 2015.

The coaches that have followed Hird — John Worsfold, Ben Rutten and Scott — have all enjoyed success at other clubs like McVeigh has, but lacked an ability to truly connect with the club and its fans.

That is McVeigh's superpower. He connects, and he connects with all generations.

It was not by accident that the club filmed McVeigh being greeted at The Hangar by Ken Fraser, the captain of Essendon's 1965 premiership side.

It was also not by accident that both McVeigh and Welsh continually referenced the goal for Essendon to be "one club", making a pointed note to invest in the club's AFLW program.

McVeigh even appeared on a podcast with some of Essendon's biggest content creators from outside the club, a stark difference from Scott, who gave off the vibe of an untouchable CEO fans could never really connect with, rather than your friendly local head coach.

Matthew Lloyd (centre) has indicated he would potentially join McVeigh (left) and Welsh (right) back at Essendon. (Getty Images: Mark Dadswell)

It is no surprise that McVeigh's arrival has already seemingly caused a change in tune from both Hird and fellow Essendon icon, Matthew Lloyd.

Since his retirement at the end of 2009, Lloyd has mostly stayed away from the club while becoming one of the AFL's most prominent media figures.

Lloyd is uncompromising when it comes to his views on Essendon, annoying segments of the club's fanbase who wonder why he has not stepped in to help fix the problems he keeps highlighting.

As McVeigh's appointment grew closer, Lloyd curiously changed his tune and said he would like to go back to club land.

It would be no surprise to see him in an official role at Essendon in the coming years as McVeigh builds out his staff.

All of this brings us back to Hird and Essendon's seemingly never-ending quest to find unity.

The basic pitch from Hird's supporters is that he is the only one who can truly bring unity back to what has been a broken club.

The pitch just missed one thing.

Who says Hird can only bring unity as Essendon's coach?

World.title: Pogačar's sensational solo attack squeezes Vuelta rivals dry
World.content:
Four days is all it took for Tadej Pogačar to end the Vuelta a España as a meaningful contest, the Slovenian great once again riding away from the peloton to win solo and establish a massive lead over the rest of the field.

It has been 32 years since Tony Rominger led a grand tour from start to finish when he won the 1994 Vuelta.

But with yet another thrilling display of daring, Pogačar put himself in pole position to emulate the Swiss rider and become just the ninth man to lead a three-week race from start to finish.

Superlatives have long been superfluous when writing about this Slovenian superstar.

Things that should not be possible are made to look routine.

When he hits the front of a race as the road goes into the mountains, the rest of the pack knows that their only chance is to ride at their own tempo.

Any attempt to fly too close to this generation's greatest star will surely send their hopes of finishing the race crashing to the ground, like Icarus.

As soon as Tadej Pogačar is in this position, that's likely to be the last the peloton sees of him. (Getty Images: Tim de Waele)

Pogačar took off with just over 50 kilometres remaining of the 104.8km circuit around Andorra la Vella to claim yet another dominant victory.

Decathlon CMA CGM put the power down at the bottom of the Collada de Beixalis climb, the second mountain of the day, and ripped the peloton to shreds.

Australian Jay Vine led the charge in support for the Slovenian's UAE Emirates XRG team, but with the pace already high, Pogačar upped his rate to burst clear.

Decathlon's Austrian leader Felix Gall tried to match Pogačar's pace in the initial throes of his attack.

However, the Austrian, as so many riders have discovered before him, could barely hold the double-world champion's wheel and quickly dropped off before being joined by the rest of the favourites.

"The pace was already super fast on the throttle right from the base [of the climb]," Pogačar told media after the race.

"When Jay let me pass him on Decathlon's wheel, I knew: 'OK, I don't want to get isolated from all those general classification contenders, because otherwise they'll all gang up on me.'

"I tried to attack on the climb. When I saw that I could open up a gap, I just hoped I could hold on until the finish. It worked out.

"It was really tough, but it's a wonderful feeling."

Tadej Pogačar is irresistable. (Getty Images: Alexander Hassenstein)

Pogačar's lead extended to over 3 minutes at one stage before he rolled home to win by 2 minutes and 39 seconds from Jarno Widar, with Gall third.

The 50km attack was his longest in a grand tour, bettering the 43km solo victory he launched in the Pyrenees last month at the Tour de France.

It is another remarkable performance from the Slovenian to add to the extraordinary wins that have become so normal it is expected of him.

Why these people believe in 'freak' Tadej Pogačar's victories As Tadej Pogačar continues to mop up cycling's biggest accolades and most controversial record, one former doper believes he's found the answer to his success: he is just a "freak".

With two key objectives to come this season, the World Championships road race in Canada falls just two weeks after the Vuelta's conclusion, with the Giro di Lombardia a further two weeks after that, Pogačar may now be able to take things easier through the next two-and-a-half weeks of racing in Spain.

The 27-year-old's lead in the general classification now stands at 3 minutes and 21 seconds, with four-time Vuelta winner Primož Roglič sitting second.

"To be honest, any lead is a bonus," Pogačar said.

"This is fantastic, because now I can head into the coming days with peace of mind and a lot of confidence.

"We're taking it day by day and staying focused. Hopefully, after this stage, the pressure will ease up a bit."

Pogačar is also a comprehensive leader in the points and king of the mountains classifications.

Wednesday's fifth stage is a hilly 173.3km ride from Falset Costa Daurada to Terres de l'Ebre in Spain's north east.

World.title: Ex-NBA player who claims to be a woman banned by WNBA team after joust
World.content:
The Chicago Sky has banned Enes Kanter Freedom from its home games after the former NBA centre was ejected from Sunday's (Monday AEST) loss to the Indiana Fever.

Owner Michael Alter made the announcement at a rare news conference on Tuesday, local time. Alter told reporters Kanter Freedom is not allowed inside Wintrust Arena for Sky games "unless sometime in the future, he's able to prove to us that he's able to abide by our rules without being a potential threat".

Kanter Freedom was removed from Sunday's game after a confrontation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter.

Cunningham's trans stance opens WNBA up to its latest hijacking atempt Sophie Cunningham insists she wants to protect the sanctity of women's sport, but her comments have opened her league up to an unprecedented attack.

Kanter Freedom was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female".

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then chest-bumped teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning and walking in Kanter Freedom's direction.

Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Kanter Freedom, 34, as she approached him. Kanter Freedom, who was standing, held his arms out and stepped onto the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved between the two.

"It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and see how much attention he could get," Alter told reporters from the Chicago Sun-Times and other media outlets.

Kanter Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby.

He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing the arena.

"I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN!" Kanter Freedom wrote on social media. "Let that sink in, AMERICA!"

Kanter Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. But a person familiar with the decision told the AP on Monday, local time, that they are not eligible. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitive nature of the situation.

The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.

Although the league's collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

AP

World.title: CTE study finds 70pc of head impacts happening in sports practice
World.content:
At least one in four former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 was found to have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), according to a new study.

Out of the 878 former players who died during that timeframe 235 donated their brains, researchers said, with 215 of those donated brains found to have CTE.

The study's lead author Daniel Daneshvar, the chair of physical medicine and rehabilitation at Mass General Brigham and an associate professor at Harvard Medical School, said it was difficult to determine how common CTE was as it could only be diagnosed after death.

"People who donate their brains are more likely to donate if they have some concern, some reason for donating, if they think that either they or a loved one is having problems with their memory or thinking or concentration or behaviour changes," he told ABC News Breakfast.

Former NFL players donated their brains to the study and 215 out of 235 were found to have CTE. (Getty Images: Nic Antaya)

"And so you can't just look at the rate of CTE amongst people who donate to get a sense of how common this disease is."

Dr Daneshvar said the "possible prevalence of CTE" among NFL players was "very concerning".

"In the general population, less than 1 per cent of people get this disease pathology in their brain," he said.

" What we found is, at a minimum, 25 per cent of these NFL players died with this disease process. "

The study from Mass General Brigham, Boston University, and the Concussion & CTE Foundation also found dementia was common among brain donors, with researchers urging prevention measures that focus on cutting down on repetitive head impacts across all levels of the sport.

"Similarly, we and others have shown that in NFL players, specifically, there is about a four times higher rate of death from neurodegenerative disease than the general population," Dr Daneshvar said.

"The bulk of the head impacts that these former NFL players experienced didn't occur at the NFL level.

Here's what we know about CTE The brain disease is caused by repeated head injuries. It's most commonly associated with athletes in contact sports, but there's a lot researchers are still trying to learn about it.

"They occurred at the collegiate level ... and at the high school level and in many cases the youth level.

" And all of those cumulative hits to the head added up to result in an increased risk. "

The NFL's 2011 Collective Bargaining Agreement limited the number of contact practices during the season. The Ivy League banned full-contact tackling during practices five years later.

The Supreme Court cleared the way for the NFL's settlement of concussion-related lawsuits with thousands of retired players in 2016.

An NFL spokesperson said the league continuously strives to make the game of football safer, "including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts".

"The NFL remains committed to ensuring that the NFL community has access to a robust — and expanding — set of resources to enhance their physical and mental wellbeing," they said.

"We encourage former players to utilise these resources to identify and seek treatment when they are concerned about their health."

Dr Daneshvar urged current and former athletes experiencing cognitive symptoms to seek a neurodegenerative disease expert evaluation.

"If the changes that have been implemented at the NFL level, including reducing the amount of contact in sports practices to less than one per week, were propagated at the collegiate, high school, and youth levels, athletes would be better off," he said.

"We know that nearly 70 per cent of head impacts are occurring in practice.

"So without changing a single minute of game time at any of those levels, we can be substantially reducing the cumulative head impact burden that these individuals are experiencing throughout their lives."

ABC/Reuters

World.title: Tomic's main draw drought continues as Australians struggle at US Open
World.content:
Bernard Tomic's seemingly unending quest to fight his way back into another grand slam main draw has fallen short once again at Flushing Meadows despite one more worthy scrap from the veteran Australian.

The last time the 33-year-old managed to battle into a main draw of a major was at his home Australian Open in 2021.

In the five years since, he has entered 10 more qualifying events in the slams and failed to negotiate his way through any.

Alas for the former teenage wonder boy who got to number 17 in the world a decade ago, that drought continued on Tuesday afternoon, local time, in New York as he fought back in his first-round match against South African Lloyd Harris only to be outplayed in the final stanza.

No-one can possibly fault the effort of world number 179 Tomic, who was once perceived as being a talented but undisciplined figure who did not really care enough about the sport, as he has since battled on in the lower reaches of the game around the world, tirelessly seeking another day in the sun.

Emerson Jones also failed in her bid to advance to the women's main draw despite a valiant fight. (AAP: Darren England)

But Harris, a former world number 31 himself who is still dangerous even if his ranking has fallen to 139, just had a little too much for the Gold Coast veteran, who staged a second-set fightback before going down 6-2, 5-7, 6-2.

It was the same story for a couple of other Australians in first-round action, as teenager Emerson Jones fought valiantly to peg back Dutch world number 164 Suzan Lamens in a tight second-set tiebreak, only to succumb in the decider 7-5, 6-7 (7-9), 6-2 after two hours and 25 minutes.

With another veteran, Alex Bolt, losing 7-6 (7-3), 7-5 to Spain's Pablo Llamas Ruiz, it meant that Australia were still looking for their first winner of the week in qualifying after James McCabe's loss on the opening Monday.

At least one Aussie was guaranteed a place in the second round of qualifying as Storm Hunter took on her friend Maddison Inglis later in the day.

AAP

Tech.title: Being a mom is hard — the heat is making it harder.
Tech.content:
It’s 8:52 AM and 86 degrees Fahrenheit (30 Celsius) where I live in Southern California. My husband just came back from a morning outing with our four-month-old. “How was the botanic garden?” I ask him. “It was okay. It was just too hot,” he tells me. I didn’t expect us to spend so much of our son’s first summer cooped up inside, hiding from the heat.

As I write this, an extreme heat warning for my area is glaring at me from my phone, effective for at least the next three days. “Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures up to 110 [degrees Fahrenheit] expected,” my weather app warns me. “Stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of the sun.”

As I write this, an extreme heat warning for my area is glaring at me from my phone.

It’s the sort of warning more kids are growing up with as global average temperatures climb. Around the world, 560 million children under the age of 10 are experiencing at least one additional month of heat stress each year as a result of climate change, according to a new study published in the journal Science Advances.

“I hope that this increases public awareness that climate change is a problem that is already happening today, that’s already affecting us,” says Rosa Pietroiusti, lead author of the study and a PhD researcher at Vrije Universiteit Brussel. “It’s affecting the health of the most vulnerable.”

Pietroiusti’s team used an international standard for moderate heat stress, days when taking protective measures like rest breaks are recommended to prevent heat-related illness. The threshold is set at a WetBulb Globe Temperature of 28 degrees Celsius (82.4 F), a measure that takes heat, humidity, wind speed, and cloud cover into account. Thanks to advances in climate attribution science, they were able to assess the number of days crossing that threshold and how many of those heat stress days were added by climate change.

They found that children are disproportionately exposed to dangerous heat, as compared to older age categories. Climate change has led to at least one additional month of heat stress for 43 percent of all kids in the 0-9 age group — 560 million little ones. That’s nearly triple the number of people aged 60-69 exposed to the same amount of climate-induced heat stress.

That’s due to even more socio-political inequity at a global scale; the highest increases in heat stress due to human-caused climate change take place in countries in the Global South that have contributed least to the fossil fuel pollution raising temperatures. These countries have younger populations, and they also tend to have less access to air conditioning or infrastructure designed to withstand extreme weather events. And if countries blow past the targets they agreed upon in the Paris climate accord, the number of children under the age of 10 that are exposed to an extra month of heat stress rises to 650 million with just 2 degrees Celsius of global warming, the new study finds.

Heat in particular can sneak up on you because it doesn’t always arrive with the same public safety warnings as a big storm might. And yet it’s a leading cause of weather related deaths globally, according to the World Health Organization. Heat stress can lead to dehydration, heat stroke, and eventually organ failure.

Babies and kids are even more susceptible than most adults. Their small bodies have a higher surface area-to-body mass ratio that makes it easier for them to overheat. Think of a small ice cube melting in the sun compared to a big block of ice. Babies’ sweat glands are still developing, making it even harder for them to regulate their body temperature. They’re totally dependent on adults to take life-saving precautions, like staying hydrated.

Heat-related illness is preventable as long as a kid can find a place to stay cool. And we can stop summers from getting even hotter than they already are today by turning to energy sources like solar and wind that don’t emit planet-heating pollution.

There are already plenty of ways the heat makes being a new mom even harder than it needs to be. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that parents avoid taking babies outside for long stretches whenever the ‘feels like’ temperature reaches higher than 90 degrees Fahrenheit (32.2 Celsius). With this summer’s heatwaves, that meant that my family was mostly stuck indoors from about 11:00 in the morning or earlier until past sunset.

My son typically loves walks outside, and spending time outdoors can be especially beneficial for a parent’s mental wellbeing postpartum. I hate that it’s not even safe to explore his grandparents’ backyard after a certain time. Sometimes there’s a doctor’s appointment or groceries to grab midday. That often means blasting the AC to cool down a sweltering car while we wait in a hot parking lot.

As irritating as this all is, I’m one of the lucky parents with a car and air conditioning at home. We had a taste of what it would be like without AC when we lost power one hot July afternoon. Power outages have grown longer in the US as extreme weather has become more common. Heatwaves can trigger blackouts because of electricity demand peaks when people blast the AC, or when utility companies preemptively shut off power lines to keep them from sparking wildfires.

Regardless of the weather, breastfeeding is hard!

My family packed up to head to grandma’s house to stay cool, and to save the stash of breastmilk in the freezer (thankfully the lights came back on just before we were about to leave). I calculated, and had the milk gone bad, that would amount to about 20 hours of my time pumping (much of it during sleepless nights) down the drain. I didn’t know this until I was about to become a mom, but newborns shouldn’t drink water. So they might feed more frequently to hydrate. Breastfeeding parents are often thirsty because you’re losing fluid to your baby, even more so in the heat.

Regardless of the weather, breastfeeding is hard! Being a parent is hard! Being a kid gets tough, too. That’s what makes lazy summer days at the beach, and having other outdoor adventures so important. It’s supposed to be an escape, and prime time for core memory-making.

Before my baby was born in April, I daydreamed about us lounging at the beach this summer. I couldn’t imagine his face yet, but I could picture those tiny toes in the sand. My son and I did manage to make it to the ocean. A baby’s skin is too sensitive for sunscreen until about 6 months old, so he wore his little blue bucket hat for a short walk along the pier. My husband took a quick video of us when I attempted to take him out of the stroller to gaze over the water. He scowls and fusses when the bright sun hits his eyes. “This is too much?” I ask him. “This is too much.”

Tech.title: The Switch 2’s $50 price increase is happening next week
Tech.content:
is an editor covering deals and gaming hardware. He joined in 2018, and after a two-year stint at Polygon, he rejoined The Verge in May 2025.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

This is a friendly reminder that the Nintendo Switch 2 will jump in price by $50 starting on September 1st. That’s next Tuesday! The company gave plenty of notice, but the time has finally come. The base 256GB model that ships without a game will go from $449.99 to $499.99. Nintendo recently announced two bundles (both well over $500) shipping this fall that include a game with a slight discount.

If you’re on the fence for a Switch 2, now is a pretty good time to buy one — not just because of the upcoming price increase. The game library is stellar and growing quickly, and the console itself is great, too. You’ll need one to play the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, The Duskbloods, and plenty of other upcoming games.

Not that the Switch 2 was ever cheap, but it was one of a few devices left out there that didn’t quickly get more expensive due to RAMageddon. Alas, no tech product will escape RAMageddon unscathed, especially one like the Switch 2 that has speedy RAM and storage. Almost all competing handhelds cost more than before, too, though Nintendo’s $50 price increase is soft compared to the $200-plus increase for the Steam Deck OLED .

And, in case you were wondering, we’ve tested some great Switch 2 accessories, and have put our favorites into respective articles that deliver multiple options. We landed on the best cases, the best screen protectors, and the best controllers, too.

Tech.title: Apple Maps has ads now
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Ads have started popping up in Apple Maps, following Apple’s announcement in March that it would let businesses pay for top spots. They’re appearing on my iPhone as the first entry in the “suggested places” section in search, but Apple says they’ll also show up at the top of search results. According to 9to5Mac, the ads began rolling out this week, and more users in the US and Canada will start seeing them over the next few weeks.

They’re marked with a blue “ad” icon, similar to the ads Google’s had in its Maps app for years now. I was also greeted with a pop-up warning me about the ads when I launched the Maps app this morning:

Maps may show local ads based on your approximate location, current search terms, or view of the map while you search. For your privacy, advertising information is not linked to your Apple Account.

Apple shared similar privacy claims in its March announcement for the ads, stating, “A user’s location and the ads they see and interact with in Maps are not associated with a user’s Apple Account. Personal data stays on a user’s device, is not collected or stored by Apple, and is not shared with third parties.”

Tech.title: Google’s new AI transcription edits out your ‘ums’ and ‘ahs’
Tech.content:
is a news writer focused on creative industries, computing, and internet culture. Jess started her career at TechRadar, covering news and hardware reviews.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Google has updated Gemini Audio with new transcription capabilities that automatically detect specialized jargon and more than 85 languages. Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is a new addition to the Gemini family that follows the launch of 3.5 Live Translate, and comes as we’re still waiting for Google to release the Gemini 3.5 Pro model that it promised to roll out in June.

Google says that 3.5 Transcribe “represents a major advancement from our previous transcription model, Chirp 3,” especially regarding multilingual performance and wording error rates. The transcription model allows users to “edit naturally with just your voice,” according to Google, and can automatically format text and remove filler words like “um” and “uh.”

Users can provide a customized vocabulary to the model, allowing 3.5 Transcribe to automatically adapt transcription to unique spelling requirements and specialized jargon to prevent those words from being edited manually. It can also attribute speech for up to three speakers in pre-recorded audio, alongside providing word-level timestamps.

Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is rolling out starting today in English for all macOS Gemini app users, and the Rambler dictation feature on Android in select countries and languages. It’s also available for developers in public preview in the Gemini API via AI Studio and Antigravity. Google says that Chrome support is coming soon.

Update, August 26th: Google also mentioned two additional Gemini Audio models, 3.5 Live, and 3.5 Live Experimental, in information provided to The Verge prior to publication, but now says that only 3.5 Transcribe is being announced today.

Tech.title: Apple announces September iPhone launch event
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Apple’s next launch event will take place on September 9th at 1PM ET. Invites to the event, which has a “Surprise and shine” tagline, were sent out on Wednesday. The event will take place at the Steve Jobs Theater in Apple Park, but there will also be a livestream on Apple’s website.

September’s show could be a big one, as Apple may finally announce the long-rumored foldable iPhone. A photo of an apparent dummy unit indicates the foldable may have a wide form factor that’s similar to what Samsung used with the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a phone that our reviewer Dominic Preston said “feels like the future.”

Apple is also expected to refresh its Pro and Pro Max phones, but those are rumored to be iterative upgrades and not a big redesign like Apple announced last year. Should past trends continue, they’ll likely be called the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

However Apple reportedly won’t announce the base model iPhone 18 at the event and instead introduce it next year. In 2027, Apple is also rumored to be launching an iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air.

This event will also be the first with John Ternus as Apple’s CEO. Formerly the company’s hardware chief, Ternus is set to take over from Tim Cook on September 1st.

Tech.title: Volvo’s cars will warn one another about hazards in the road
Tech.content:
is transportation editor with 10+ years of experience who covers EVs, public transportation, and aviation. His work has appeared in The New York Daily News and City & State.

Volvo is updating three of its electric vehicles with new hazard alerts to warn drivers when there are animals or vulnerable road users ahead. The new connected safety features are based on Volvo’s cars talking to one another, as opposed to crowdsourced alert systems used by popular navigation tools like Google Maps and Waze.

The alerts work by using connected vehicle data from Volvo’s fleet of passenger vehicles in Europe, the US, and Canada. The car’s sensors and cameras are tuned to identify certain risks on the road. When one Volvo spots a hazard, it automatically logs the location and sends it to Volvo’s servers. Alerts are then sent to all other Volvo vehicles traveling along that same road. The alerts still depend on the car being connected to the cloud and the road existing in the map database, but Volvo’s newer EVs have plenty of computing power to handle the real-time processing requests.

Previous Next









1 / 6

Volvo said it’s updating its EVs with alerts for four types of hazards: large animals; vulnerable road users, like pedestrians or cyclists; roadwork; and accidents. The new alerts are coming to the Volvo EX90, ES90, and EX60. Volvo says it has 1 million vehicles on the road today with connected safety alert capabilities. And it shares its alert data with traffic management centers, as well as other vehicle brands, so its not just Volvo branded vehicles that are benefiting.

Volvo has used connected vehicle technology to power some of its hazard warnings since 2016. The Swedish company’s cloud-based system, developed in partnership with Ericsson, warns drivers of slippery roads ahead based on feedback from steering, braking, and acceleration sensors. It also notifies nearby vehicles when another car has activated its hazard lights indicating that another driver may be in a dangerous or unexpected position on the road.

In addition, Volvo said that the EX90 would be getting Spatial Audio support for Apple CarPlay users. This will allow drivers to “enjoy a multi-dimensional and immersive sound experience that places music and vocals around the cabin,” the company says.

Tech.title: Xbox announces disc-to-digital feature that digitizes your physical games
Tech.content:
Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Microsoft is officially announcing a new Xbox feature that will allow Xbox owners to digitize their existing physical game collections. The disc-to-digital feature, which The Verge exclusively revealed last month, is part of work that Microsoft is doing for game preservation and in preparation for the next generation of Xbox consoles.

“Most Xbox One and Xbox Series X disc-based games support this new feature,” explains Jason Ronald, VP of next generation at Xbox. “Players can claim a digital entitlement by inserting a supported disc into an Xbox One or Xbox Series X console and launching the game.” This digital entitlement is tied to the specific disc, and it will move from account to account if you swap the physical game with a friend or log in to a different Xbox profile and try to play a disc-based game.

Microsoft will start testing this new Xbox disc-to-digital feature with Xbox Insider testers on August 31st, followed by a broader rollout to Xbox One and Xbox Series X consoles in the coming months. Once you have a digital version of an Xbox disc game, if supported you’ll also be able to access the game on PC through Xbox Play Anywhere, or stream it to multiple devices with Xbox Cloud Gaming.

A leaked memo from earlier this month revealed that publishers would have control over the Xbox disc-to-digital, so not every game will be supported initially. “We’re starting with thousands of titles, and we’ll continue to add more over time,” says Ronald. “While not every title will be available at launch, this is an important step toward a future where players can have greater confidence that the games they buy remain with them for years to come.”

The Xbox disc-to-digital feature arrives just weeks after Sony announced it’s killing all physical PlayStation game discs. New PlayStation games released after January 2028 will be digital-only, but it’s not yet clear if Microsoft will announce a similar end of production for Xbox discs. Either way, Sony hasn’t announced a similar feature for converting an existing physical library into a digital one.

Microsoft is also bringing Xbox and Xbox 360 games to PC, in a move that could allow the next Xbox console to play every Xbox game ever made.

Tech.title: US seizes domains of Chinese botnet used to hack NASA, Justice Department, and the Senate
Tech.content:
The FBI has seized a series of domains that were used by a large-scale botnet to coordinate and launch China-backed cyberattacks against American targets.

According to the Justice Department’s statement on Wednesday, the seizures of the botnet’s domains deny the operators access to the platforms. The botnet was allegedly used by the Chinese government to break into computers across the United States, including systems at hospitals, defense contractors, and several federal government departments.

Prosecutors said the China state-sponsored group, known as QTFY, was run by a Chinese company called Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Tech, which created and operated the botnet of thousands of compromised internet-connected devices. The botnet aimed to serve as obfuscation networks, which hide the malicious traffic of hackers to make their activity more difficult to detect.

Per the Justice Department, QTFY offers computer hacking services to its customers, who include Chinese government hackers working for the Ministry of State Security, and allows them to use the botnet.

The hacks date back to 2018, and affected NASA, the Federal Reserve, and the Departments of Energy, Justice, and Health and Human Services. The U.S. Senate was compromised as recently as 2026, according to the government’s affidavit seeking a court order to seize the botnet’s domains filed earlier this week.

The Justice Department said that the domain seizures made the botnet and its command and control servers “inoperable,” as the domains were hardcoded into the botnet’s code, and were critical for the botnet’s communication and essential operations.

Network giant Lumen said in a blog post that it had observed the hackers profiling and targeting government agencies, the defense and aerospace sectors, and others for the past year, and shared threat intelligence with the FBI.

Tech.title: Capital F closes $17M debut fund with goal to back the future of the ‘female economy’
Tech.content:
Capital F, one of the few all-female-led VC firms, announced Wednesday the $17 million close of its debut fund.

The firm backs companies building in the “female economy” — or the markets where women drive demand. That mainly falls into three buckets for the firm, Margaret Coblentz, the firm’s co-founder, told TechCrunch — women’s health, digital commerce, and AI tools. The latter is increasingly important since “women are disproportionately the victims of trust and safety violations,” Dawn Dobras, the co-founder of Capital F, added.

Coblentz and Dobras spent the last 30 years running companies together. Dobras was notably the CEO of the clean beauty retailer Credo Beauty and spent a decade at Gap before moving on to the clothing retailer Charlotte Russe. Coblentz also worked at Charlotte Russe before launching her own luxury knitwear brand, which eventually exited.

Coblentz said she and Dobras decided to come together and launch a firm after spending years at the executive top ranks and realizing that “there weren’t a lot of women there.”

“If you had asked me maybe 15 years ago, ‘are you going to go into venture?’ I don’t know that I would have said yes,” Coblentz said. She and Dobras started angel investing after their corporate careers, and always knew that “who writes the check and who owns the company matters quite a bit.” They first worked together almost 17 years ago at Charlotte Russe and figured, well, second time was the charm.

The result was Capital F, named after their favorite F words, Dobras said. “Things like future, fund, fantastic, and, you know, fill in the blank.”

During the fundraising process, they hosted salon events across the country for the “VC curious” to bring more women into investing, and as a result, almost 80% of the fund’s LPs are women, including Jenny Ming, the CEO of Rothys and former head of Old Navy, Marta Benson, former CEO of Pottery Barn, and Linnesa Roberts and her firm Gingerbread Capital.

“We realized that many times women aren’t invited into the rooms to invest in funds,” Dobras said.

Dobras said Capital F doesn’t back a founder until they’ve spoken to at least two of their 10 LPs. “We’ve seen those relationships move into advisor, into board members, into additional investments,” she continued, “and most importantly, lots and lots of sales introductions.”

The journey to raise this fund had its ups and downs. “We always say we’re going to write a book,” Dobras said. They were working with the disadvantage of essentially being new fund managers. “Really, the people who supported us and wrote those checks came out of those salons,” Dobras said.

Over the past decade, there has been a lot of talk about the importance of investing in more technology that centers women’s issues, such as women’s health, which has long been underfunded and underfocused. Coblentz said that, in many ways, those conversations have led to some innovations that are starting to have an impact. They also mentioned companies in their portfolio, like Malama, which offers doula support for people on Medicaid.

The firm has cut checks to 13 companies. It backs early-stage companies, writing checks between $250,000 and $1 million. Portfolio companies include the telemedicine startup Hey Jane, the hormone-tracking platform Stardust, and Steller Sleep, which Google acquired last year. “That was a fun LP letter to write because we hadn’t even closed the fund and we’ve already had an exit,” Dobras said.

They expect to finish deploying the fund by the end of 2027.

Tech.title: Meta agrees to sweeping changes to restrict kids’ access to its apps as part of settlement with states
Tech.content:
Under the terms of its $18 billion settlement to resolve claims brought by 29 U.S. states over children’s safety, Meta on Wednesday agreed to sweeping changes designed to restrict minors’ access to Instagram and Facebook. The changes include a daily time limit, a restrictive “Night Mode,” autoplay controls, and more.

The social media giant says the new protections will automatically apply to users under 18 on Instagram and Facebook in participating U.S. states and territories, pending judicial approval. That the majority of these controls are required to remain in place for 10 years.

One of the most notable changes is that Meta plans to implement a daily two-hour time limit for teenagers on its platform. The limit can only be disabled with parental permission, and once the limit is reached, teens will be locked out of Facebook and Instagram.

Meta says the limit will be cumulative across Facebook and Instagram, which means that time spent on both apps will count toward the two-hour total. The limit will also be applied if Meta detects someone is using multiple accounts.

The company also said kids will be able to choose a non-algorithmic feed that isn’t personalized by its recommendation systems as their default. Currently, users have been able to temporarily see a chronological feed on Instagram and Facebook, but can’t set it as their default feed. Instead, the app pops up the algorithmic feeds each time you open the app. Now, parents and guardians can set their teenaged kids’ default experience to a non-personalized feed.

Meta said it will also introduce a default “Night Mode” block on its apps between midnight and 6 a.m. that would prevent underage users from accessing, posting or viewing any part of its platforms. A Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch that while the company already mutes notifications for teens at night, the new setting will block them altogether after midnight.

Teenagers will also receive prompts after every 15 minutes of continuous usage on Facebook or Instagram. The new prompts will accompany the current prompts that teens see when their total daily usage hits 60 minutes.

Meta will also block underage users from using extreme makeup filters, a move that expands upon its existing restrictions that prevent them from using cosmetic surgery filters.

Additionally, the company will mute notifications by default during school timings, which it is setting as between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. During those hours, teens won’t receive push notifications, except for DMs and alerts related to account security or safety.

Another new setting will allow parents and teens to turn off autoplay. Meta says they will need to take a “deliberate action,” such as tapping or swiping, to see more content.

Like and reaction counts on posts will also be hidden for underage users by default, whether the posts are theirs or someone else’s. While teens can already choose to hide like counts, now those counts will be hidden by default.

Meta also said it’s strengthening its technology for identifying users who may be aged 13 to 17, even if they provide an adult birth date, to ensure they receive appropriate protections.

The social media giant published an open letter asking TikTok and YouTube to join it in setting an industry-wide commitment by also introducing a daily time limit, turning off access to apps at night, restricting notifications during school hours, and 15-minute usage prompts.

Meta’s $18 billion settlement will be distributed to the states over 10 years, but 30% of the settlement, or about $5.3 billion, will only be paid if YouTube and TikTok implement the same limits.

“All platforms should empower parents and support teens by putting the same measures in place, because we know that when teens are restricted on one app, they simply move to another,” the company wrote in a blog post.

Meta said it will continue to prevent teens from following or interacting with accounts it considers age-inappropriate. It will also continue to default teens into private accounts and restrict suspicious adults from contacting them.
